```ts
// Parsed requests of the scripted Anthropic Messages API (design 15.1). Scripts answer from what a request carries
// (its session, its newest tool results, the user's words, markers from the brief), never from the order requests
// arrive in, so everything here is read from one request alone.
//
// What 2.1.285 sends, as seen in the probes: the session id in X-Claude-Code-Session-Id and in metadata.user_id; the
// system prompt as text blocks; the brief as user context, not in system; after each tool_result a separate user
// message of context; and a message pushed mid-turn as a role 'system' entry in the message list.

export type AnthropicRole = 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system';

export interface AnthropicToolResult {
  toolUseId: string;
  /** The result's text blocks joined by newlines; other blocks (images) are left out. */
  text: string;
  isError: boolean;
}

export type AnthropicBlock =
  | { type: 'text'; text: string }
  | { type: 'tool_use'; id: string; name: string; input: unknown }
  | ({ type: 'tool_result' } & AnthropicToolResult)
  /** Thinking, images and anything newer, by their type only. */
  | { type: 'other'; kind: string };

export interface AnthropicMessage {
  role: AnthropicRole;
  blocks: AnthropicBlock[];
}

export interface AnthropicRequest {
  /** The request path without its query (2.1.285 adds ?beta=true). */
  path: string;
  endpoint: 'messages' | 'count_tokens' | 'other';
  /** From X-Claude-Code-Session-Id, else from metadata.user_id. */
  sessionId: string | null;
  model: string | null;
  stream: boolean;
  /** The system prompt's text. */
  system: string;
  messages: AnthropicMessage[];
  /** Names of the offered tools. */
  tools: string[];
  /** The tool results after the last assistant message: what the model is now answering. */
  toolResults: AnthropicToolResult[];
  /** The newest of toolResults, or null when the newest input holds none (a new prompt, say). */
  lastToolResult: AnthropicToolResult | null;
  /** Texts of the user and system entries after the last assistant message: a prompt, messages folded in mid-turn. */
  userTexts: string[];
  /** A request of the agent's own loop, which a script answers; auxiliary ones get the server's default. */
  mainLoop: boolean;
  /** A request for a compaction summary. */
  compaction: boolean;
  /** Lower-case header names. */
  headers: Record<string, string>;
  /** The JSON body as received. */
  body: unknown;
}

type HeadersLike = Headers | Record<string, string>;

/** Every compaction prompt of 2.1.285 (full, partial and from-the-start summaries) contains this. */
const COMPACTION_MARKER = 'Your task is to create a detailed summary of';

const UUID = /[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}/i;

function record(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> {
  return value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value)
    ? (value as Record<string, unknown>)
    : {};
}

function lowerCaseHeaders(headers: HeadersLike): Record<string, string> {
  const entries = headers instanceof Headers ? [...headers.entries()] : Object.entries(headers);
  return Object.fromEntries(entries.map(([name, value]) => [name.toLowerCase(), value]));
}

/** metadata.user_id is JSON with a session_id in 2.1.285; older CLIs used `user_<hash>_account_<id>_session_<uuid>`. */
function sessionFromMetadata(metadata: unknown): string | null {
  const userId = record(metadata).user_id;
  if (typeof userId !== 'string') return null;
  try {
    const sessionId = record(JSON.parse(userId)).session_id;
    if (typeof sessionId === 'string' && sessionId) return sessionId;
  } catch {
    // Not JSON: the older form below.
  }
  return userId.match(new RegExp(`session_(${UUID.source})`, 'i'))?.[1] ?? null;
}

function textOf(content: unknown): string {
  if (typeof content === 'string') return content;
  if (!Array.isArray(content)) return '';
  return content
    .map(record)
    .filter((block) => block.type === 'text' && typeof block.text === 'string')
    .map((block) => block.text as string)
    .join('\n');
}

function parseBlock(value: unknown): AnthropicBlock {
  const block = record(value);
  switch (block.type) {
    case 'text':
      return { type: 'text', text: typeof block.text === 'string' ? block.text : '' };
    case 'tool_use':
      return { type: 'tool_use', id: String(block.id ?? ''), name: String(block.name ?? ''), input: block.input ?? {} };
    case 'tool_result':
      return {
        type: 'tool_result',
        toolUseId: String(block.tool_use_id ?? ''),
        text: textOf(block.content),
        isError: block.is_error === true,
      };
    default:
      return { type: 'other', kind: typeof block.type === 'string' ? block.type : 'unknown' };
  }
}

function parseMessage(value: unknown): AnthropicMessage {
  const message = record(value);
  const role: AnthropicRole = message.role === 'assistant' || message.role === 'system' ? message.role : 'user';
  const content = message.content;
  if (typeof content === 'string') return { role, blocks: [{ type: 'text', text: content }] };
  return { role, blocks: Array.isArray(content) ? content.map(parseBlock) : [] };
}

function endpointOf(path: string): AnthropicRequest['endpoint'] {
  if (path === '/v1/messages') return 'messages';
  if (path === '/v1/messages/count_tokens') return 'count_tokens';
  return 'other';
}

/** Whether a request asks for a compaction summary. */
export function isCompaction(request: Pick<AnthropicRequest, 'userTexts'>): boolean {
  return request.userTexts.some((value) => value.includes(COMPACTION_MARKER));
}

/**
 * Whether a request belongs to the agent's own loop: a Messages request that offers tools and is no compaction.
 * Titles, summaries and other auxiliary requests offer none.
 */
export function isMainLoop(request: Pick<AnthropicRequest, 'endpoint' | 'tools' | 'userTexts'>): boolean {
  return request.endpoint === 'messages' && request.tools.length > 0 && !isCompaction(request);
}

/** Parses a request body (JSON, any shape) and its headers; path is the request path without its query. */
export function parseAnthropicRequest(
  body: unknown,
  headers: HeadersLike = {},
  path: string = '/v1/messages',
): AnthropicRequest {
  const fields = record(body);
  const lowered = lowerCaseHeaders(headers);
  const messages = Array.isArray(fields.messages) ? fields.messages.map(parseMessage) : [];
  const lastAssistant = messages.findLastIndex((message) => message.role === 'assistant');
  const newest = messages.slice(lastAssistant + 1);
  const toolResults = newest.flatMap((message) =>
    message.blocks.flatMap((block) =>
      block.type === 'tool_result' ? [{ toolUseId: block.toolUseId, text: block.text, isError: block.isError }] : [],
    ),
  );
  const userTexts = newest.flatMap((message) =>
    message.blocks.flatMap((block) => (block.type === 'text' ? [block.text] : [])),
  );
  const tools = Array.isArray(fields.tools)
    ? fields.tools.map(record).flatMap((tool) => (typeof tool.name === 'string' ? [tool.name] : []))
    : [];
  const endpoint = endpointOf(path);
  const sessionHeader = lowered['x-claude-code-session-id'];
  return {
    path,
    endpoint,
    sessionId: sessionHeader || sessionFromMetadata(fields.metadata),
    model: typeof fields.model === 'string' ? fields.model : null,
    stream: fields.stream === true,
    system: textOf(fields.system),
    messages,
    tools,
    toolResults,
    lastToolResult: toolResults.at(-1) ?? null,
    userTexts,
    mainLoop: isMainLoop({ endpoint, tools, userTexts }),
    compaction: isCompaction({ userTexts }),
    headers: lowered,
    body,
  };
}
```

```ts
// Encodes a scripted reply the way the Messages API sends it: an event stream for streaming requests, one JSON message
// otherwise. Text and tool input arrive in several deltas, as from the real API, so clients reassemble them.
import type { ContentBlock, MessageReply } from './replies';

export interface EncodeOptions {
  /** The message id, msg_… */
  id: string;
  /** The model the request named. */
  model: string;
}

/** Characters per delta. */
const CHUNK = 24;

/** Splits by code points, so no delta ends in half of a surrogate pair. */
function chunks(value: string): string[] {
  const points = Array.from(value);
  const parts: string[] = [];
  for (let start = 0; start < points.length; start += CHUNK) parts.push(points.slice(start, start + CHUNK).join(''));
  return parts.length > 0 ? parts : [''];
}

function usageOf(reply: MessageReply) {
  return {
    input_tokens: reply.usage.inputTokens,
    output_tokens: reply.usage.outputTokens,
    cache_creation_input_tokens: 0,
    cache_read_input_tokens: 0,
  };
}

function event(name: string, data: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  return `event: ${name}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify({ type: name, ...data })}\n\n`;
}

function blockEvents(block: ContentBlock, index: number): string[] {
  if (block.type === 'text') {
    return [
      event('content_block_start', { index, content_block: { type: 'text', text: '' } }),
      ...chunks(block.text).map((text) =>
        event('content_block_delta', { index, delta: { type: 'text_delta', text } }),
      ),
      event('content_block_stop', { index }),
    ];
  }
  return [
    event('content_block_start', {
      index,
      content_block: { type: 'tool_use', id: block.id, name: block.name, input: {} },
    }),
    ...chunks(JSON.stringify(block.input)).map((partial_json) =>
      event('content_block_delta', { index, delta: { type: 'input_json_delta', partial_json } }),
    ),
    event('content_block_stop', { index }),
  ];
}

/** The reply as the API's server-sent events, from message_start to message_stop. */
export function encodeSse(reply: MessageReply, options: EncodeOptions): string {
  const usage = usageOf(reply);
  return [
    event('message_start', {
      message: {
        id: options.id,
        type: 'message',
        role: 'assistant',
        model: options.model,
        content: [],
        stop_reason: null,
        stop_sequence: null,
        usage: { ...usage, output_tokens: 1 },
      },
    }),
    ...reply.content.flatMap(blockEvents),
    event('message_delta', { delta: { stop_reason: reply.stopReason, stop_sequence: null }, usage }),
    event('message_stop', {}),
  ].join('');
}

/** The reply as one JSON message, for requests that do not stream. */
export function encodeMessage(reply: MessageReply, options: EncodeOptions): Record<string, unknown> {
  return {
    id: options.id,
    type: 'message',
    role: 'assistant',
    model: options.model,
    content: reply.content,
    stop_reason: reply.stopReason,
    stop_sequence: null,
    usage: usageOf(reply),
  };
}
```

### Task 3: Scripted Anthropic Messages server

`startScriptedAnthropic` serves `POST /v1/messages` (streamed or not) and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on 127.0.0.1 and returns `{ url, port, requests, unmatched, setHandler, release, close }`, the shape X-20 fixes for both scripted servers (design 15.1). The handler gets each parsed request and returns a reply or nothing. Nothing gets a harmless default: `AUXILIARY_TEXT` for auxiliary requests (titles, summaries) and `UNSCRIPTED_TEXT` for main-loop requests, which also go to `unmatched`, as do unknown routes and bodies that are not JSON, so new request kinds show up. A held reply delays the whole response until `release(gate)`, and `close()` ends held requests. `anthropic/index.ts` is the entry M2d's tests and M2g's harness import; the testkit's main index and package.json stay untouched (X-44).

**File:** `packages/testkit/src/anthropic/server.ts` (new)

```ts
// The scripted Anthropic Messages API (design 15.1, X-20). The real claude reaches it through ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so
// adapter tests, the recorder and M2g's cluster run real CLI turns with zero model use. It has the shape both scripted
// servers share: { url, requests, setHandler }, with parsed requests and a harmless default answer.
import { type AnthropicRequest, parseAnthropicRequest } from './request';
import { type AnthropicReply, type ErrorReply, fail, type MessageReply, reply, scriptedId } from './replies';
import { encodeMessage, encodeSse } from './sse';

/** Answers a parsed request, or declines it with nothing so the server's default answers. */
export type AnthropicHandler = (
  request: AnthropicRequest,
) => AnthropicReply | undefined | Promise<AnthropicReply | undefined>;

/** The default answer to a main-loop request no script answered; it ends the turn. */
export const UNSCRIPTED_TEXT = 'agflow scripted server: no scripted reply for this request.';
/** The default answer to auxiliary requests: titles, summaries and the like. */
export const AUXILIARY_TEXT = 'ok';

export interface ScriptedAnthropic {
  /** http://127.0.0.1:<port>, for ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. */
  url: string;
  port: number;
  /** Every request, parsed and with its raw headers and body, in arrival order. */
  requests: AnthropicRequest[];
  /** Main-loop requests the handler declined, and requests the server could not serve. */
  unmatched: AnthropicRequest[];
  /** Replaces the handler for later requests; null declines everything. */
  setHandler(handler: AnthropicHandler | null): void;
  /** Lets every reply held on the gate through, now and later. */
  release(gate: string): void;
  /** Ends held requests and stops the server. */
  close(): Promise<void>;
}

export interface ScriptedAnthropicOptions {
  handler?: AnthropicHandler;
}

interface Gate {
  open: boolean;
  waiters: (() => void)[];
}

function errorResponse(error: ErrorReply): Response {
  return Response.json(error.body, {
    status: error.status,
    headers: { 'request-id': scriptedId('req'), ...error.headers },
  });
}

function messageResponse(message: MessageReply, request: AnthropicRequest): Response {
  const options = { id: scriptedId('msg'), model: request.model ?? 'claude-scripted' };
  const headers = { 'request-id': scriptedId('req'), ...message.headers };
  if (request.stream) {
    return new Response(encodeSse(message, options), {
      headers: { 'content-type': 'text/event-stream; charset=utf-8', 'cache-control': 'no-cache', ...headers },
    });
  }
  return Response.json(encodeMessage(message, options), { headers });
}

/** A rough count, as no tokenizer is at hand: four characters a token. */
function countTokens(raw: string): number {
  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil(raw.length / 4));
}

export async function startScriptedAnthropic(options: ScriptedAnthropicOptions = {}): Promise<ScriptedAnthropic> {
  const requests: AnthropicRequest[] = [];
  const unmatched: AnthropicRequest[] = [];
  const gates = new Map<string, Gate>();
  let handler: AnthropicHandler | null = options.handler ?? null;
  let closed = false;

  function gate(name: string): Gate {
    let found = gates.get(name);
    if (!found) {
      found = { open: false, waiters: [] };
      gates.set(name, found);
    }
    return found;
  }

  function openGate(name: string): void {
    const found = gate(name);
    found.open = true;
    for (const wake of found.waiters.splice(0)) wake();
  }

  /** Resolves true once the gate opens, false when the server closes first. */
  function passGate(name: string): Promise<boolean> {
    const found = gate(name);
    if (found.open || closed) return Promise.resolve(!closed);
    return new Promise((resolve) => found.waiters.push(() => resolve(!closed)));
  }

  async function answer(request: AnthropicRequest): Promise<Response> {
    let scripted: AnthropicReply | undefined;
    try {
      scripted = handler ? await handler(request) : undefined;
    } catch (error) {
      return errorResponse(fail(500, { message: `the scripted handler threw: ${(error as Error).message}` }));
    }
    if (scripted === undefined) {
      if (request.mainLoop) unmatched.push(request);
      scripted = reply(request.mainLoop ? UNSCRIPTED_TEXT : AUXILIARY_TEXT);
    }
    if (scripted.kind === 'hold') {
      // A request still held at close() gets no answer: stopping the server drops its connection.
      if (!(await passGate(scripted.gate))) return new Response(null, { status: 503 });
      scripted = scripted.then;
    }
    return scripted.kind === 'error' ? errorResponse(scripted) : messageResponse(scripted, request);
  }

  const server = Bun.serve({
    hostname: '127.0.0.1',
    port: 0,
    // Held replies may wait as long as a test needs.
    idleTimeout: 0,
    async fetch(incoming) {
      const path = new URL(incoming.url).pathname;
      const raw = await incoming.text();
      let body: unknown = raw;
      let parsed = raw === '';
      if (raw !== '') {
        try {
          body = JSON.parse(raw);
          parsed = true;
        } catch {
          // Recorded as the raw text below.
        }
      }
      const request = parseAnthropicRequest(body, incoming.headers, path);
      requests.push(request);
      if (request.endpoint === 'other' || incoming.method !== 'POST') {
        unmatched.push(request);
        return errorResponse(fail(404, { message: `the scripted server has no route ${incoming.method} ${path}` }));
      }
      if (!parsed) {
        unmatched.push(request);
        return errorResponse(fail(400, { message: 'the request body is not JSON' }));
      }
      if (request.endpoint === 'count_tokens') return Response.json({ input_tokens: countTokens(raw) });
      return answer(request);
    },
  });

  return {
    url: `http://127.0.0.1:${server.port}`,
    port: server.port as number,
    requests,
    unmatched,
    setHandler(next) {
      handler = next;
    },
    release: openGate,
    async close() {
      if (closed) return;
      closed = true;
      for (const found of gates.values()) for (const wake of found.waiters.splice(0)) wake();
      await server.stop(true);
    },
  };
}
```

### Task 4: Claude test environment and the pinned-binary locator

Pieces every Claude test shares and M2g reuses (design 15, 15.1, X-20). `claudeTestEnv` builds runner.json's `test.claudeEnv`: the scripted server as `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, the fake `CLAUDE_TEST_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES` (0 unless a test asks), the switches that stop non-essential traffic, and the refusing proxy for every other host. `findClaudeBinary(version)` looks at `AGFLOW_CLAUDE_BIN`, then `~/.agflow/runner/vendor/claude/<version>/claude` under the real home (never `AGFLOW_HOME`), keeps only a binary whose `--version` is that version, and otherwise says why and how to get one; it is synchronous, so a test file can decide at load time whether to skip. `linkClaudeBinary` links a located binary into a test runner home's `vendor/` and never deletes the binary it was given. The testkit's anthropic entry imports no runner code, so `binary-layout.test.ts` checks from the runner side that the layout and the version format match `vendorBinary` and `parseVendorVersion`.

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { chmodSync, mkdtempSync, realpathSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';

import { join } from 'node:path';
import { findClaudeBinary, linkClaudeBinary } from '@agflow/testkit/src/anthropic';

import { runnerPaths } from '../../../src/paths';
import { parseVendorVersion, vendorBinary } from '../../../src/vendor/pins';

const dirs: string[] = [];
afterEach(() => {
  for (const dir of dirs.splice(0)) rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

function tempDir(): string {
  const dir = realpathSync(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-claude-layout-')));
  dirs.push(dir);
  return dir;
}

/** Tests that run a new stub get room for macOS's slow first exec of a new file, more so under load. */
const STUB_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;

/**
 * A claude stand-in that prints `<stub>.out`, so one file (one slow first exec) serves every output. The path is
 * written in, because the stub also runs through a link.
 */
function stub(output: string): string {
  const bin = join(tempDir(), 'claude');
  writeFileSync(bin, `#!/bin/sh\ncat '${bin}.out'\n`);
  chmodSync(bin, 0o755);
  writeFileSync(`${bin}.out`, `${output}\n`);
  return bin;
}
```

```ts
    });
    expect(CLAUDE_TEST_API_KEY).toStartWith('sk-ant-');
  });

    const env = claudeTestEnv({ baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:1', proxyUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:2', maxRetries: 2 });
    expect(env.CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES).toBe('2');

  test('a Messages request made with it reaches the scripted server, and external hosts hit the proxy', async () => {
    const server = await startScriptedAnthropic({ handler: () => reply('through the scripted server') });
    servers.push(server);
    const proxy = await startRefusingProxy();
    proxies.push(proxy);
    // A child process gets the environment the way the CLI does: requests follow its proxy variables.
    const script = `
      const env = process.env;
      const response = await fetch(env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + '/v1/messages', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'x-api-key': env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY },
        body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'claude-sonnet-5-5', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] }),
      });
      const message = await response.json();
      // A reserved host: should the proxy variables be ignored, the request fails at DNS and reaches nothing.
      const external = await fetch('https://agflow-test.invalid/v1/messages', { method: 'POST' }).then(
        (r) => r.status,
        () => 'failed',
      );
      console.log(JSON.stringify({ status: response.status, text: message.content[0].text, external }));
    `;
    const env = claudeTestEnv({ baseUrl: server.url, proxyUrl: proxy.url });
    const child = Bun.spawn([process.execPath, '-e', script], {
      env: { PATH: process.env.PATH ?? '/usr/bin:/bin', ...env },
      stdout: 'pipe',
      stderr: 'pipe',
    });
    const [stdout, stderr] = await Promise.all([
      new Response(child.stdout).text(),
      new Response(child.stderr).text(),
    ]);
    expect({ code: await child.exited, stderr }).toEqual({ code: 0, stderr: '' });
    const outcome = JSON.parse(stdout);
    expect(outcome).toMatchObject({ status: 200, text: 'through the scripted server' });
    expect([403, 'failed']).toContain(outcome.external);
    expect(server.requests).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(server.requests[0]?.headers['x-api-key']).toBe(CLAUDE_TEST_API_KEY);
    // The proxy saw only the external host, never the scripted server.
    expect(proxy.refused.map((refused) => refused.target)).toEqual(['agflow-test.invalid:443']);
  });
});
```

**File:** `packages/testkit/src/anthropic/binary.ts` (new)

```ts
// The pinned claude for tests (design 15, X-20). Tests never download it: they use AGFLOW_CLAUDE_BIN, or the runner's
// vendor directory under the real home, which `bun run vendor:install` fills. The testkit imports no runner code, so
// the layout (vendorBinary) and the version format (parseVendorVersion) are followed by convention; a runner-side test
// holds them together.
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, realpathSync, rmSync, symlinkSync } from 'node:fs';
import { homedir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';

export type ClaudeBinaryLookup = { path: string; reason: null } | { path: null; reason: string };

export interface FindClaudeBinaryOptions {
  /** process.env by default. */
  env?: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  /** The home whose ~/.agflow/runner/vendor is searched; the real home by default, whatever AGFLOW_HOME says. */
  home?: string;
  /** For each `--version`; 10 s by default. */
  timeoutMs?: number;
}

const VERSION = /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/;
const VERSION_OUTPUT = /^(\d+\.\d+\.\d+) \(Claude Code\)$/;

/** Where vendorBinary('claude', version) lies under an AGFLOW_HOME. */
function vendorClaude(agflowHome: string, version: string): string {
  if (!VERSION.test(version)) throw new Error(`not a vendor version: ${JSON.stringify(version)}`);
  return join(agflowHome, 'runner', 'vendor', 'claude', version, 'claude');
}

/** Why a candidate is not the pinned binary, or null when it is. */
function candidateProblem(path: string, version: string, timeoutMs: number): string | null {
  if (!existsSync(path)) return 'is missing';
  let result: Bun.SyncSubprocess<'pipe', 'ignore'>;
  try {
    // `--version` needs no home or configuration; nothing but PATH is passed.
    result = Bun.spawnSync([path, '--version'], {
      env: { PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin' },
      stdin: 'ignore',
      stdout: 'pipe',
      stderr: 'ignore',
      timeout: timeoutMs,
    });
  } catch (error) {
    return `cannot run: ${(error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code ?? (error as Error).message}`;
  }
  if (result.exitedDueToTimeout) return 'did not answer --version';
  const found = result.exitCode === 0 ? result.stdout.toString().trim().match(VERSION_OUTPUT)?.[1] : undefined;
  if (found === undefined) return 'has an unreadable version';
  return found === version ? null : `is claude ${found}`;
}

/**
 * The pinned claude of a version: AGFLOW_CLAUDE_BIN, then ~/.agflow/runner/vendor/claude/<version>/claude. Only a
 * binary whose `--version` reports the version counts; otherwise the reason names each candidate and the remedy.
 * Synchronous, so a test file can decide at load time whether its suite runs.
 */
export function findClaudeBinary(version: string, options: FindClaudeBinaryOptions = {}): ClaudeBinaryLookup {
  const env = options.env ?? process.env;
  const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? 10_000;
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const explicit = env.AGFLOW_CLAUDE_BIN;
  if (explicit) {
    const problem = candidateProblem(explicit, version, timeoutMs);
    if (problem === null) return { path: explicit, reason: null };
    problems.push(`AGFLOW_CLAUDE_BIN ${explicit} ${problem}`);
  } else {
    problems.push('AGFLOW_CLAUDE_BIN is not set');
  }
  const vendored = vendorClaude(join(options.home ?? homedir(), '.agflow'), version);
  const problem = candidateProblem(vendored, version, timeoutMs);
  if (problem === null) return { path: vendored, reason: null };
  problems.push(`${vendored} ${problem}`);
  return {
    path: null,
    reason:
      `no claude ${version}: ${problems.join('; ')}. ` +
      `Set AGFLOW_CLAUDE_BIN to a claude ${version} binary, or run \`bun run vendor:install\`.`,
  };
}

/** Links a located binary into a test runner home's vendor directory, where the runner looks; returns the link. */
export function linkClaudeBinary(agflowHome: string, version: string, bin: string): string {
  const link = vendorClaude(agflowHome, version);
  // The binary findClaudeBinary found under this very home is already in place; replacing it would delete it.
  if (resolve(bin) === link || (existsSync(link) && existsSync(bin) && realpathSync(link) === realpathSync(bin))) {
    return link;
  }
  mkdirSync(dirname(link), { recursive: true });
  rmSync(link, { force: true });
  symlinkSync(resolve(bin), link);
  return link;
}
```

```ts
// runner.json's test.claudeEnv for a test (design 15.1, X-20): the CLI talks to the scripted Messages API with a fake
// key, never retries unless a test asks, sends no non-essential traffic, and reaches every other host only through the
// refusing proxy, which records the attempt.

/** A key the scripted server accepts; it is no real key and reaches no real API. */
export const CLAUDE_TEST_API_KEY = 'sk-ant-api03-agflow-test-dummy-key';

export interface ClaudeTestEnvOptions {
  /** The scripted server's url. */
  baseUrl: string;
  /** The refusing proxy's url. */
  proxyUrl: string;
  /** CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES, 0 by default so an error reaches the adapter at once. */
  maxRetries?: number;
}

export function claudeTestEnv(options: ClaudeTestEnvOptions): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: options.baseUrl,
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: CLAUDE_TEST_API_KEY,
    CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES: String(options.maxRetries ?? 0),
    CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC: '1',
    DISABLE_TELEMETRY: '1',
    DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING: '1',
    HTTPS_PROXY: options.proxyUrl,
    HTTP_PROXY: options.proxyUrl,
    // The scripted server and the test hub listen on the loopback interface and are reached directly.
    NO_PROXY: '127.0.0.1,localhost',
  };
}
```

### Task 5: Shell words and the Bash verdict

The first half of section 8.2's PreToolUse guard. `splitShellCommands` is a small recursive-descent POSIX shell lexer: it lists every simple command a line would run (inside subshells, command and process substitutions, backticks and unquoted here-documents) with its redirections, and never expands anything. `bashVerdict` refuses `git push` in every form (`git -C … push`, `send-pack`, `http-push`, `subtree push`, aliases, `rebase --exec`), `git credential`, `git config --global`, `gh`, `glab` and `security`, also behind wrappers (`env`, `command`, `xargs`, `timeout`, `sudo`, …), `sh -c`, `eval` and `find -exec`, and writes into `.git/hooks` or `.git/config`. Names and `.git` paths compare case-folded as APFS does, and a command it cannot parse, or whose name is computed when it runs (`$g`, `$(echo git)`), is refused. The network boundary stays the control (design 5); this layer refuses at once what would fail there anyway. Refuse computed Git subcommands as well as computed program names. The real CLI executed `v=push; git "$v"` and `git "$(printf push)"` despite `CLAUDE_PUSH_DENY_RULES`. `bashVerdict` rejects unresolved dollar/backtick expansion in the Git subcommand, including recursively parsed eval and shell commands. Computed data arguments, such as `git -C "$repo" status` and `git log --format="$format"`, remain allowed.

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { bashVerdict } from '../../../src/adapters/claude/bash-verdict';

const GIT_WRITE = 'writing into .git/hooks or .git/config is refused';

function reason(command: string): string {
  const verdict = bashVerdict(command);
  if (verdict.allow) throw new Error(`expected ${JSON.stringify(command)} to be refused`);
  return verdict.reason;
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { type ShellCommand, splitShellCommands } from '../../../src/adapters/claude/shell-words';

/** The commands of a line that must parse, as their words. */
function words(line: string): string[][] {
  return commands(line).map((command) => command.words);
}

function commands(line: string): ShellCommand[] {
  const split = splitShellCommands(line);
  if (!split.ok) throw new Error(`expected ${JSON.stringify(line)} to parse: ${split.problem}`);
  return split.commands;
}

function problem(line: string): string {
  const split = splitShellCommands(line);
  if (split.ok) throw new Error(`expected ${JSON.stringify(line)} not to parse`);
  return split.problem;
}

describe('splitShellCommands', () => {
  test('words lose their quotes and escapes', () => {
    expect(words(`git commit -m "push later" 'it''s' a\\ b \\git ""`)).toEqual([
      ['git', 'commit', '-m', 'push later', 'its', 'a b', 'git', ''],
    ]);
    expect(words(`echo "a \\"b\\" \\$c \\x" $'tab\\tq\\'s'`)).toEqual([['echo', 'a "b" $c \\x', "tab\tq's"]]);
    expect(words('echo one\\\ntwo')).toEqual([['echo', 'onetwo']]);
  });

  test('operators and newlines separate commands', () => {
    expect(words('a 1; b 2 && c || d | e & f\ng |& h')).toEqual([
      ['a', '1'],
      ['b', '2'],
      ['c'],
      ['d'],
      ['e'],
      ['f'],
      ['g'],
      ['h'],
    ]);
    expect(words('a;b&&c')).toEqual([['a'], ['b'], ['c']]);
    expect(words('  ;; \n')).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('comments end at the line end, but # inside a word is kept', () => {
    expect(words('a # git push\nb c#d')).toEqual([['a'], ['b', 'c#d']]);
  });

  test('subshells, groups and function bodies contribute their commands', () => {
    expect(words('(cd x && git push) | cat')).toEqual([['cd', 'x'], ['git', 'push'], ['cat']]);
    expect(words('{ a; b; }')).toEqual([['{', 'a'], ['b'], ['}']]);
    expect(words('f() { git push; }; f')).toEqual([['f'], ['{', 'git', 'push'], ['}'], ['f']]);
  });

  test('command substitutions and backticks are parsed as commands of their own', () => {
    expect(words('echo $(git push) done')).toEqual([['git', 'push'], ['echo', '$(git push)', 'done']]);
    expect(words('echo "x $(a "q" | b) y"')).toEqual([['a', 'q'], ['b'], ['echo', 'x $(a "q" | b) y']]);
    expect(words('echo `git push` "`b`"')).toEqual([['git', 'push'], ['b'], ['echo', '`git push`', '`b`']]);
    expect(words('echo $(a $(b) `c`)')).toEqual([['b'], ['c'], ['a', '$(b)', '`c`'], ['echo', '$(a $(b) `c`)']]);

    expect(problem('echo `git push')).toBe('unterminated backtick');
    expect(problem('echo ${A')).toBe('unterminated ${');

    expect(problem('a )')).toBe('unexpected )');
    expect(problem('a >')).toBe('a redirection without a target');
    expect(problem('a && && b')).toBe('unexpected &&');
    expect(problem('echo \\')).toBe('a trailing backslash');
    expect(problem(`echo ${'$('.repeat(100)}x${')'.repeat(100)}`)).toBe('nested too deeply');
    const nestings: [string, string][] = [

      ['$((', '))'],
      ['"${', '}"'],
      ['${"', '"}'],

    for (const [open, close] of nestings) {
      expect(problem(`echo ${open.repeat(100)}x${close.repeat(100)}`)).toBe('nested too deeply');

      expect(problem(`echo ${open.repeat(20_000)}x${close.repeat(20_000)}`)).toBe('nested too deeply');

    expect(words("$'\\x67it' $'\\147' $'\\u00e9' $'\\cA'")).toEqual([['git', 'g', 'é', '\x01']]);
  });
});
```

```ts
// The guard's verdict on Bash commands (design 8.2, boundaries 1 and 4 of section 5). The network boundary is the
// control: agents have no route to the git host and no credentials. This layer refuses the commands that would only
// make sense if one of those failed, so a refusal tells the agent at once instead of after a network timeout.
import { posix } from 'node:path';
import { type ShellRedirect, splitShellCommands } from './shell-words';

export type Verdict = { allow: true } | { allow: false; reason: string };

const ALLOW: Verdict = { allow: true };

/** sh -c inside eval inside sh -c …: past this depth the command is refused as unparseable. */
const MAX_DEPTH = 16;

class Unparseable extends Error {}

export function bashVerdict(command: string): Verdict {
  try {
    const reason = judgeScript(command, 0);
    return reason === null ? ALLOW : { allow: false, reason };
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof Unparseable) {
      return { allow: false, reason: `the command cannot be parsed (${error.message}), so it is refused` };
    }
    throw error;
  }
}

const GIT_WRITE_REFUSED = 'writing into .git/hooks or .git/config is refused';

/**
 * A name as macOS's case-insensitive volumes compare it, the fold core's protected paths use: `GIT` runs git and
 * `.GIT/Hooks` is .git/hooks there. Decomposing turns the Kelvin sign into K, and upper-casing between two
 * lower-casings folds ſ to s and ı to i.
 */
export function foldCase(text: string): string {
  return text.normalize('NFD').toLowerCase().toUpperCase().toLowerCase();
}

function judgeScript(source: string, depth: number): string | null {
  if (depth > MAX_DEPTH) throw new Unparseable('shells nested too deeply');
  const split = splitShellCommands(source);
  if (!split.ok) throw new Unparseable(split.problem);
  for (const command of split.commands) {
    const reason = judgeRedirects(command.redirects) ?? judgeWords(command.words, command.redirects, depth);
    if (reason !== null) return reason;
  }
  return null;
}

const WRITING_REDIRECTS = new Set(['>', '>>', '>|', '&>', '&>>', '<>']);

function judgeRedirects(redirects: ShellRedirect[]): string | null {
  for (const { op, target } of redirects) {
    // >&2 duplicates a descriptor; >&file (any other word) writes the file.
    const writes = WRITING_REDIRECTS.has(op) || (op === '>&' && !/^(\d+|-)$/.test(target));
    if (writes && writesGitFile(target)) return GIT_WRITE_REFUSED;
  }
  return null;
}

/** Keywords that may precede a command name in a simple command as the lexer splits it. */
const RESERVED = new Set(['!', '{', '}', 'if', 'then', 'elif', 'else', 'while', 'until', 'do']);
const ASSIGNMENT = /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\+?=/;

function judgeWords(words: string[], redirects: ShellRedirect[], depth: number): string | null {
  let start = 0;
  for (;;) {
    const word = words[start];
    // `function f { …; }`, zsh's `repeat 3 …` and bash's `coproc NAME { …; }` put one word before the command.
    if (word === 'function' || word === 'repeat' || (word === 'coproc' && RESERVED.has(words[start + 2] ?? ''))) {
      start += 2;
    } else if (word !== undefined && (RESERVED.has(word) || word === 'coproc')) start += 1;
    else break;
  }
  return judgeArgv(words.slice(start), redirects, depth);
}

/**
 * Commands that run their arguments as a command, with the options that take a value. Anything else that starts with
 * a dash is a flag. `positionals` counts the arguments between the options and the command (timeout's duration).
 */
const WRAPPERS: Record<string, { valued: string[]; positionals?: number }> = {
  // zsh's precommand modifiers; zsh is the default shell the Bash tool runs commands in on macOS.
  '-': { valued: [] },
  noglob: { valued: [] },
  nocorrect: { valued: [] },
  builtin: { valued: [] },
  exec: { valued: ['-a'] },
  nohup: { valued: [] },
  time: { valued: [] },
  nice: { valued: ['-n', '--adjustment'] },
  timeout: { valued: ['-s', '-k', '--signal', '--kill-after'], positionals: 1 },
  gtimeout: { valued: ['-s', '-k', '--signal', '--kill-after'], positionals: 1 },
  sudo: {
    valued: ['-u', '-g', '-h', '-p', '-C', '-D', '-r', '-t', '-U', '-T', '--user', '--group', '--host', '--prompt'],
  },
  doas: { valued: ['-u', '-C'] },
  xargs: {
    valued: ['-I', '-J', '-L', '-n', '-P', '-s', '-E', '-d', '-R', '-S', '-a', '--arg-file', '--delimiter'],
  },
  stdbuf: { valued: ['-i', '-o', '-e', '--input', '--output', '--error'] },
  caffeinate: { valued: ['-t', '-w'] },
  setsid: { valued: [] },
  arch: { valued: [] },
};

const SHELLS = new Set(['sh', 'bash', 'zsh', 'dash', 'ksh', 'mksh', 'fish']);

/** Every git command that sends objects to a remote. */
const GIT_PUSHERS = new Set(['push', 'send-pack', 'http-push']);
/** git's own options before the subcommand that take a separate value. */
const GIT_VALUED = new Set([
  '-C',
  '-c',
  '--git-dir',
  '--work-tree',
  '--namespace',
  '--super-prefix',
  '--config-env',
  '--attr-source',
]);

const REFUSED_PROGRAMS: Record<string, string> = {
  gh: 'gh is refused: agents reach the hub only through the agflow tools',
  glab: 'glab is refused: agents reach the hub only through the agflow tools',
  security: 'security is refused: agents may not use the keychain',
};

/**
 * A simple command's words after the keywords. `redirects` are the command's own, which a shell started without a
 * script reads its script from.
 */
function judgeArgv(argv: string[], redirects: ShellRedirect[], depth: number): string | null {
  let start = 0;
  while (start < argv.length && ASSIGNMENT.test(argv[start] as string)) start += 1;
  const program = argv[start];
  if (program === undefined) return null;
  // zsh expands `=git` to git's path; case-insensitive volumes find `GIT` as git.
  const name = foldCase(posix.basename(program.replace(/^=/, '')));
  // `$g push` or `$(echo git) push` names its program only when it runs, so the guard cannot judge it.
  if (/[$`]/.test(name)) throw new Unparseable(`the command name ${program} is computed when it runs`);
  const args = argv.slice(start + 1);
  const refused = REFUSED_PROGRAMS[name];
  if (refused !== undefined) return refused;
  if (name === 'git') return judgeGit(args, depth);
  if (name.startsWith('git-')) return judgeGitSubcommand(name.slice(4), args, depth);
  if (name === 'env') return judgeEnv(args, redirects, depth);
  if (name === 'command') return judgeCommandBuiltin(args, redirects, depth);
  if (name === 'eval') return judgeScript(args.join(' '), depth + 1);
  if (SHELLS.has(name)) return judgeShell(name, args, redirects, depth);
  if (name === 'find') return judgeFind(args, depth);
  if (name === 'cp' || name === 'mv' || name === 'ln' || name === 'install') return judgeCopy(name, args);

function writesGitFile(path: string): boolean {
  const normal = foldCase(posix.normalize(path));

  return `'${word.replaceAll("'", `'\\''`)}'`;
}
```

```ts
// A small POSIX shell lexer for the guard's Bash verdict (design 8.2). It finds every simple command a command line
// would run, including those inside subshells, command and process substitutions, backticks and unquoted
// here-documents, and the redirections each one makes. It never expands anything: a word keeps the source text of its
// expansions, so `$(git push)` is both a command of its own and the literal text of the word that holds it.

export interface ShellRedirect {
  /** One of < > >> >| <> <& >& &> &>> << <<- <<<. */
  op: string;
  /** The explicit file descriptor (`2>`), or null. */
  fd: number | null;
  /** The target word without quotes; for here-documents, the delimiter. */
  target: string;
  /** A here-document's body (with <<-, its leading tabs removed): a shell given no script reads it as one. */
  body?: string;
}

export interface ShellCommand {
  words: string[];
  redirects: ShellRedirect[];
}

export type ShellSplit = { ok: true; commands: ShellCommand[] } | { ok: false; problem: string };

class ShellSyntaxError extends Error {}

/** Deeper nesting than this is no command a person or an agent writes; it is refused rather than recursed into. */
const MAX_NESTING = 64;

const REDIRECT_OPS = ['&>>', '&>', '<<<', '<<-', '<<', '<>', '<&', '>>', '>&', '>|', '<', '>'];
const CONTROL_OPS = ['&&', '||', '|&', '|', ';', '&'];
/** Operators that need a command on their left. */
const BINARY_OPS = new Set(['&&', '||', '|&', '|']);
const WORD_END = new Set([' ', '\t', '\n', ';', '&', '|', '(', ')', '<', '>']);

const ANSI_C_DIGITS: Record<string, RegExp> = {
  x: /^[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,2}/,
  u: /^[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,4}/,
  U: /^[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,8}/,
};

/**
 * Splits a command line into the simple commands it runs, in the order their parsing completes: a substitution's
 * commands come before the command whose word holds it. A line that is not valid shell gives the problem instead.
 */
export function splitShellCommands(source: string): ShellSplit {
  const commands: ShellCommand[] = [];
  try {
    new Parser(source, commands, 0).script();
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ShellSyntaxError) return { ok: false, problem: error.message };
    throw error;
  }
  return { ok: true, commands };
}

interface PendingHereDoc {
  /** The << or <<- redirection whose body this is. */

  delimiter: string;

interface Word {

class Parser {

  constructor(

        a: '\x07',
        b: '\b',
        e: '\x1b',
        E: '\x1b',
        f: '\f',
        v: '\v',
        '\\': '\\',
        "'": "'",
        '"': '"',
        '?': '?',
      };
      if (e in simple) value += simple[e];
      else if (e === 'x' || e === 'u' || e === 'U' || /[0-7]/.test(e)) {
        const digits = this.src.slice(this.pos).match(ANSI_C_DIGITS[e] ?? /^[0-7]{0,2}/)?.[0] ?? '';
        this.pos += digits.length;
        const code = /[0-7]/.test(e) ? Number.parseInt(e + digits, 8) : Number.parseInt(digits || '0', 16);
        value += String.fromCodePoint(Math.min(code, 0x10ffff));
      } else if (e === 'c') {
        const control = this.src[this.pos] ?? '';
        this.pos += 1;
        value += String.fromCharCode(control.charCodeAt(0) & 0x1f);
      } else value += `\\${e}`;
    }
  }

  /** After a newline, the bodies of the here-documents that line opened, in order. */
  private readHereDocs(): void {
    for (const doc of this.pending.splice(0)) {
      let body = '';
      for (;;) {
        if (this.pos >= this.src.length) throw new ShellSyntaxError(`unterminated here-document ${doc.delimiter}`);
        const end = this.src.indexOf('\n', this.pos);
        const line = this.src.slice(this.pos, end < 0 ? this.src.length : end);
        this.pos = end < 0 ? this.src.length : end + 1;
        const content = doc.stripTabs ? line.replace(/^\t+/, '') : line;
        if (content === doc.delimiter) break;
        body += `${content}\n`;
      }
      doc.redirect.body = body;
      if (doc.expand) new Parser(body, this.out, this.depth + 1).hereDocBody();
    }
  }

  private requireNoPendingHereDocs(): void {
    const [doc] = this.pending;
    if (doc) throw new ShellSyntaxError(`unterminated here-document ${doc.delimiter}`);
  }

  private skipBlanks(): void {
    for (;;) {
      const c = this.src[this.pos];
      if (c === ' ' || c === '\t') this.pos += 1;
      else if (c === '\\' && this.src[this.pos + 1] === '\n') this.pos += 2;
      else return;
    }
  }

  private nest(): void {
    this.depth += 1;
    if (this.depth > MAX_NESTING) throw new ShellSyntaxError('nested too deeply');
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test packages/runner/test/adapters/claude/shell-words.test.ts packages/runner/test/adapters/claude/bash-verdict.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: the task's tests pass (`0 fail`); then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`) and `tsc` exits 0.

Known limits, accepted because the network boundary is the control: an inline `case … esac` is refused as unparseable, pipes into a shell and script files are not followed, and `$EDITOR file` is refused (its name is computed). `foldCase` copies core's APFS fold, which core does not export. Refuse computed Git subcommands as well as computed program names. The real CLI executed `v=push; git "$v"` and `git "$(printf push)"` despite `CLAUDE_PUSH_DENY_RULES`. `bashVerdict` rejects unresolved dollar/backtick expansion in the Git subcommand, including recursively parsed eval and shell commands. Computed data arguments, such as `git -C "$repo" status` and `git log --format="$format"`, remain allowed.

### Task 6: Guard path rules, the attempt's project directory and the hook

The second half of the guard and the PreToolUse callback for both profiles (design 8.2, 7.6, X-29). `guardDecision` refuses Edit, Write and NotebookEdit outside the clone and its temporary directory, and on `<clone>/.git/config` or under `<clone>/.git/hooks/`; Read, Glob and Grep in another attempt's clone under the work root and under `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/projects/` outside the attempt's own project directory; Bash goes to `bashVerdict`. Tool paths resolve as 2.1.285 resolves them (trimmed, `~` from the agent's `HOME`, relative to the hook input's `cwd`) and compare as real paths, so links and case tricks do not help. `paths.ts` names the project directory as the binary's sanitiser does: the clone's real path with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by '-'; a slug over 200 characters, which the CLI would hash, throws. `createGuardHook` turns any error into a deny, because Claude Code runs the tool when a callback fails.

```ts
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, realpathSync, rmSync, symlinkSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import type { HookInput, PreToolUseHookInput } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';
import { createGuardHook, type GuardScope, guardDecision } from '../../../src/adapters/claude/guard';
import { claudeProjectDir } from '../../../src/adapters/claude/paths';

interface Fixture {
  /** What afterEach removes. */
  base: string;
  /** The symlinked directory everything in the scope is reached through. */
  root: string;
  scope: GuardScope;
  /** Another attempt's clone of the same project. */
  other: string;
  /** Another attempt of the same task, whose name starts with the clone's. */
  sibling: string;
  ownProject: string;
  otherProject: string;
  siblingProject: string;
}

let fx: Fixture;

beforeEach(() => {
  // The scope reaches everything through a symlink, as macOS's /tmp -> /private/tmp does, on every platform.
  const base = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'agflow-guard-'));
  mkdirSync(join(base, 'real'));
  symlinkSync(join(base, 'real'), join(base, 'link'));
  const root = join(base, 'link');
  const home = join(root, 'home');
  const workRoot = join(home, '.agflow', 'work');
  const clone = join(workRoot, 'p', 'T-1-a1');
  const other = join(workRoot, 'p', 'T-2-b2');
  const sibling = join(workRoot, 'p', 'T-1-a10');
  const claudeHome = join(home, '.agflow', 'runner', 'homes', 'claude');
  const tmpDir = join(root, 'tmp', 'agf', 'abc123');
  // Like M2b's createTaskClone, which clones with --template=: the clone has no .git/hooks.
  for (const dir of [join(clone, '.git'), join(clone, 'src'), join(clone, 'a', 'b'), other, sibling, tmpDir]) {
    mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  }
  writeFileSync(join(clone, '.git', 'config'), '[core]\n');
  writeFileSync(join(other, 'secret.txt'), 'x');
  writeFileSync(join(sibling, 'secret.txt'), 'x');
  const ownProject = claudeProjectDir(claudeHome, clone);
  const otherProject = claudeProjectDir(claudeHome, other);
  const siblingProject = claudeProjectDir(claudeHome, sibling);
  mkdirSync(join(ownProject, 'tool-results'), { recursive: true });
  mkdirSync(otherProject, { recursive: true });
  mkdirSync(siblingProject, { recursive: true });
  fx = {
    base,
    root,
    scope: { clone, tmpDir, workRoot, claudeHome, home },
    other,
    sibling,
    ownProject,
    otherProject,
    siblingProject,
  };
});

afterEach(() => {
  rmSync(fx.base, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

function decide(tool: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, cwd?: string) {
  return guardDecision(fx.scope, tool, input, cwd);
}

function refusal(tool: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, cwd?: string): string {
  const verdict = decide(tool, input, cwd);
  if (verdict.allow) throw new Error(`expected ${tool} ${JSON.stringify(input)} to be refused`);
  return verdict.reason;
}

const EDITORS = [
  ['Edit', 'file_path'],
  ['Write', 'file_path'],
  ['NotebookEdit', 'notebook_path'],
] as const;

describe('the guard on Edit, Write and NotebookEdit', () => {
  test('they are allowed inside the clone and the temporary directory, compared as real paths', () => {
    const { clone, tmpDir } = fx.scope;
    const realClone = realpathSync(clone);
    for (const [tool, key] of EDITORS) {
      for (const path of [
        join(clone, 'src', 'a.ts'),
        join(realClone, 'src', 'a.ts'),
        join(clone, 'new', 'deeper', 'file.ts'),
        join(tmpDir, 'scratch.txt'),
        join(realpathSync(tmpDir), 'scratch.txt'),
        'src/relative.ts',
        join(clone, '.git', 'info', 'exclude'),
      ]) {
        const verdict = decide(tool, { [key]: path });
        expect({ tool, path, verdict }).toEqual({ tool, path, verdict: { allow: true } });
      }
    }
  });

  test('they are refused outside, through a symlink that points out, through .., and without a path', () => {
    const { clone } = fx.scope;
    symlinkSync(fx.root, join(clone, 'out'));
    symlinkSync(join(fx.root, 'planted.txt'), join(clone, 'dangling'));
    for (const [tool, key] of EDITORS) {
      for (const path of [
        join(fx.root, 'outside.txt'),
        join(fx.other, 'secret.txt'),
        join(clone, '..', 'T-2-b2', 'x.ts'),
        '../T-2-b2/x.ts',
        join(clone, 'out', 'x.ts'),
        join(clone, 'dangling'),
        '~/.zshrc',
        '~/.agflow/work/p/T-2-b2/x.ts',
        fx.scope.workRoot,
        join(fx.sibling, 'x.ts'),
        ` ${join(fx.other, 'x.ts')}`,
      ]) {
        expect({ tool, path, reason: refusal(tool, { [key]: path }) }).toEqual({
          tool,
          path,
          reason: `${tool} outside the clone and its temporary directory is refused`,
        });
      }
      expect(refusal(tool, {})).toBe(`${tool} without a file path is refused`);
    }
  });

  test('.git/config and everything under .git/hooks are refused, also in another spelling', () => {
    const { clone } = fx.scope;
    const paths = [
      join(clone, '.git', 'config'),
      join(clone, '.git', 'hooks'),
      join(clone, '.git', 'hooks', 'pre-commit'),
      join(clone, '.git', 'hooks', 'new', 'x'),
      join(clone, 'src', '..', '.git', 'config'),
      '.git/hooks/pre-push',
      // A case-insensitive volume (macOS by default) reaches the same files in these spellings, the Kelvin sign
      // and ſ included, even where the clone has no hooks directory yet.
      join(clone, '.GIT', 'CONFIG'),
      join(clone, '.git', 'Hooks', 'pre-commit'),
      join(clone, '.git', 'HOOKS', 'x'),
      join(clone, '.git', 'hoo\u212As', 'x'),
      join(clone, '.git', 'hook\u017F', 'x'),
    ];
    for (const [tool, key] of EDITORS) {
      for (const path of paths) {
        expect({ tool, path, reason: refusal(tool, { [key]: path }) }).toEqual({
          tool,
          path,
          reason: `${tool} on .git/config or under .git/hooks is refused`,
        });
      }
    }
    // Once a hooks directory exists in another spelling, the real path takes that spelling.
    mkdirSync(join(clone, '.git', 'Hooks'));
    expect(refusal('Write', { file_path: join(clone, '.git', 'hooks', 'pre-commit') })).toBe(
      'Write on .git/config or under .git/hooks is refused',
    );
  });
});

describe('the guard on Read, Glob and Grep', () => {
  test("another attempt's clone is refused, also through a symlink and as a search root", () => {
    const { clone, workRoot } = fx.scope;
    symlinkSync(fx.other, join(clone, 'peek'));

describe('createGuardHook', () => {
  function input(tool: string, toolInput: unknown, cwd = fx.scope.clone): PreToolUseHookInput {
    return {
      hook_event_name: 'PreToolUse',
      session_id: 's',
      transcript_path: join(fx.ownProject, 's.jsonl'),
      cwd,
      tool_name: tool,
      tool_input: toolInput,
      tool_use_id: 'toolu_1',
    };
  }

  async function call(hookInput: HookInput): Promise<unknown> {
    const matcher = createGuardHook(fx.scope);
    expect(matcher.matcher).toBeUndefined();

    if (!hook) throw new Error('the guard matcher has no hook');
    return hook(hookInput, 'toolu_1', { signal: new AbortController().signal });

  test('a refusal is a PreToolUse deny with the reason; anything else answers {}', async () => {
    expect(await call(input('Write', { file_path: join(fx.root, 'x'), content: 'x' }))).toEqual({

    });
    expect(await call(input('Write', { file_path: join(fx.scope.clone, 'x'), content: 'x' }))).toEqual({});
    expect(await call(input('Bash', { command: 'ls' }))).toEqual({});
    expect(await call({ ...input('Bash', { command: 'git push' }), hook_event_name: 'PostToolUse' } as never)).toEqual(
      {},
    );
  });

  test("relative paths resolve against the input's cwd", async () => {
    const deeper = join(fx.scope.clone, 'a', 'b');
    for (const tool of ['Grep', 'Glob']) {
      expect(await call(input(tool, { pattern: '*', path: '../../../T-2-b2' }, deeper))).toEqual({
        hookSpecificOutput: {
          hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
          permissionDecision: 'deny',
          permissionDecisionReason: `${tool} is in another attempt's clone, which is refused`,
        },
      });

    // An empty cwd falls back to the clone.
    expect(await call(input('Write', { file_path: 'x.ts', content: 'x' }, ''))).toEqual({});

  test('a call the guard cannot judge is denied, never thrown', async () => {

      get command(): string {

    expect(await call(input('Bash', throwing))).toMatchObject({
      hookSpecificOutput: {
        hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
        permissionDecision: 'deny',
        permissionDecisionReason: expect.stringMatching(/^the guard could not judge this call \(boom\)/),
      },
    });
    const deep = `git push; echo ${'"${'.repeat(16_408)}x${'}"'.repeat(16_408)}`;
    expect(await call(input('Bash', { command: deep }))).toMatchObject({
      hookSpecificOutput: { permissionDecision: 'deny' },
    });

  test('a path that cannot be resolved is refused, not thrown', async () => {
    symlinkSync('loop-b', join(fx.scope.clone, 'loop-a'));
    symlinkSync('loop-a', join(fx.scope.clone, 'loop-b'));
    expect(await call(input('Edit', { file_path: join(fx.scope.clone, 'loop-a', 'x') }))).toMatchObject({
      hookSpecificOutput: {
        permissionDecision: 'deny',
        permissionDecisionReason: expect.stringMatching(/^Edit on a path that cannot be resolved/),
      },
    });
```

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, realpathSync, rmSync, symlinkSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import {
  claudeProjectDir,
  claudeProjectSlug,
  MAX_CLAUDE_PROJECT_SLUG,
  realPathOf,
} from '../../../src/adapters/claude/paths';

const dirs: string[] = [];
afterEach(() => {
  for (const dir of dirs.splice(0)) rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

/** A temporary directory under /tmp, which macOS reaches through the /tmp -> /private/tmp symlink. */
function tmpRoot(): string {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(process.platform === 'darwin' ? '/tmp' : tmpdir(), 'agflow-slug-'));
  dirs.push(dir);
  return dir;
}

describe("Claude's project directory", () => {
  test('the slug is the real path of the clone with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by -', () => {
    const root = tmpRoot();
    const clone = join(root, 'x', '.agflow', 'work', 'p', 'T-1-a1');
    mkdirSync(clone, { recursive: true });
    const slug = claudeProjectSlug(clone);
    expect(slug).toBe(realpathSync(clone).replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, '-'));
    expect(slug.endsWith('-x--agflow-work-p-T-1-a1')).toBe(true);
    if (process.platform === 'darwin') expect(slug.startsWith('-private-tmp-agflow-slug-')).toBe(true);
    expect(claudeProjectDir('/home/claude', clone)).toBe(join('/home/claude', 'projects', slug));
  });

  test('a symlinked clone path and a not yet existing clone get the same slug as the real path would', () => {
    const root = tmpRoot();
    const real = join(root, 'work', 'p', 'T-1-a1');
    mkdirSync(real, { recursive: true });
    symlinkSync(join(root, 'work'), join(root, 'link'));
    expect(claudeProjectSlug(join(root, 'link', 'p', 'T-1-a1'))).toBe(claudeProjectSlug(real));
    expect(claudeProjectSlug(join(root, 'work', 'p', 'T-9-gone'))).toBe(
      `${realpathSync(join(root, 'work', 'p'))}/T-9-gone`.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, '-'),
    );
  });

  test('a slug over 200 characters is refused, because the CLI then appends a hash', () => {
    const root = tmpRoot();
    const base = realpathSync(root).length + 1;
    const fits = join(root, 'a'.repeat(MAX_CLAUDE_PROJECT_SLUG - base));
    expect(claudeProjectSlug(fits)).toHaveLength(MAX_CLAUDE_PROJECT_SLUG);
    expect(() => claudeProjectSlug(`${fits}b`)).toThrow(/201 characters/);
  });
});

describe('realPathOf', () => {
  test('resolves symlinks, also dangling ones, and judges a missing path by its nearest existing parent', () => {
    const root = tmpRoot();
    const real = realpathSync(root);
    mkdirSync(join(root, 'dir'));
    symlinkSync(join(root, 'dir'), join(root, 'to-dir'));
    symlinkSync(join(root, 'elsewhere', 'file'), join(root, 'dangling'));
    symlinkSync('loop-b', join(root, 'loop-a'));
    symlinkSync('loop-a', join(root, 'loop-b'));
    expect(realPathOf(join(root, 'to-dir', 'new', 'file.ts'))).toBe(join(real, 'dir', 'new', 'file.ts'));
    expect(realPathOf(join(root, 'dangling'))).toBe(join(real, 'elsewhere', 'file'));
    expect(realPathOf(join(root, 'dir', '..', 'to-dir'))).toBe(join(real, 'dir'));
    expect(() => realPathOf(join(root, 'loop-a', 'x'))).toThrow(/symbolic links/);
  });
});
```

```ts
// The PreToolUse guard, in both profiles (design 8.2, 7.6, X-29). Claude Code's in-process tools do not run in the
// sandbox, and permission rules cannot name the work root without denying the attempt's own clone, so this callback
// confines them: Edit, Write and NotebookEdit to the clone and its temporary directory, minus the clone's .git/config
// and .git/hooks; Read, Glob and Grep away from other attempts' clones and other sessions' Claude project
// directories. Bash commands get bashVerdict. Every path compares as a real path, and tool paths resolve as Claude
// Code 2.1.285 resolves them: trimmed, ~ expanded, and relative to the CLI's current directory, the hook input's cwd
// (the clone at start; a Bash `cd` inside the clone persists).
import { isAbsolute, join, resolve, sep } from 'node:path';
import type { HookCallbackMatcher, HookJSONOutput } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';
import { bashVerdict, foldCase, type Verdict } from './bash-verdict';
import { claudeProjectDir, realPathOf } from './paths';

export interface GuardScope {
  /** The attempt's clone, the agent's working directory. */
  clone: string;
  /** CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR, the attempt's private temporary directory. */
  tmpDir: string;
  /** ~/.agflow/work, which holds every attempt's clone. */
  workRoot: string;
  /** CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, whose projects/ holds every session's transcripts. */
  claudeHome: string;
  /** The agent's HOME, which the CLI expands a leading ~ to; never the runner's own. */
  home: string;
}

const ALLOW: Verdict = { allow: true };
const EDITORS: Record<string, string> = { Edit: 'file_path', Write: 'file_path', NotebookEdit: 'notebook_path' };
const READERS = new Set(['Read', 'Glob', 'Grep']);
const GLOB_CHARS = /[*?[{]/;

/** The guard's verdict on one tool call; `cwd` is the CLI's current directory, which relative paths resolve against. */
export function guardDecision(
  scope: GuardScope,
  toolName: string,
  toolInput: unknown,
  cwd: string = scope.clone,
): Verdict {
  const input = (typeof toolInput === 'object' && toolInput !== null ? toolInput : {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (toolName === 'Bash') {
    return typeof input.command === 'string'
      ? bashVerdict(input.command)
      : refuse('Bash without a command is refused');
  }
  const editorKey = EDITORS[toolName];
  if (editorKey === undefined && !READERS.has(toolName)) return ALLOW;
  try {
    if (editorKey !== undefined) {
      const path = input[editorKey];
      if (typeof path !== 'string' || path === '') return refuse(`${toolName} without a file path is refused`);
      return judgeEdit(toolName, realPathOf(toolPath(scope, cwd, path)), roots(scope));
    }
    return judgeRead(toolName, readTargets(scope, cwd, toolName, input), roots(scope));
  } catch (error) {
    return refuse(`${toolName} on a path that cannot be resolved (${(error as Error).message}) is refused`);
  }
}

/** The PreToolUse matcher for query()'s hooks: no `matcher`, so it sees every tool call. */
export function createGuardHook(scope: GuardScope): HookCallbackMatcher {
  return {
    hooks: [
      async (input): Promise<HookJSONOutput> => {
        if (input.hook_event_name !== 'PreToolUse') return {};
        let verdict: Verdict;
        try {
          verdict = guardDecision(scope, input.tool_name, input.tool_input, input.cwd || scope.clone);
        } catch (error) {
          // Claude Code runs the tool when a hook callback fails, so the guard refuses instead of throwing.
          verdict = refuse(`the guard could not judge this call (${(error as Error).message}), so it is refused`);
        }
        if (verdict.allow) return {};
        return {
          hookSpecificOutput: {
            hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
            permissionDecision: 'deny',
            permissionDecisionReason: verdict.reason,
          },
        };
      },
    ],
  };
}

interface Roots {
  clone: string;
  tmpDir: string;
  work: string;
  projects: string;
  ownProject: string;
}

function roots(scope: GuardScope): Roots {
  return {
    clone: realPathOf(scope.clone),
    tmpDir: realPathOf(scope.tmpDir),
    work: realPathOf(scope.workRoot),
    projects: realPathOf(join(scope.claudeHome, 'projects')),
    ownProject: realPathOf(claudeProjectDir(scope.claudeHome, scope.clone)),
  };
}

function judgeEdit(tool: string, path: string, root: Roots): Verdict {
  if (!within(path, root.clone) && !within(path, root.tmpDir)) {
    return refuse(`${tool} outside the clone and its temporary directory is refused`);
  }
  // Folded, as macOS volumes find .git/HOOKS as .git/hooks: a clone made with --template= has no hooks directory
  // whose real path would give the spelling.
  const gitDir = foldCase(join(root.clone, '.git'));
  const folded = foldCase(path);
  if (folded === join(gitDir, 'config') || within(folded, join(gitDir, 'hooks'))) {
    return refuse(`${tool} on .git/config or under .git/hooks is refused`);
  }
  return ALLOW;
}

/**
 * The real paths a read tool reaches: Read's file, and a search's root, which is its path (the current directory
 * when absent or blank) and, when the pattern starts with fixed directories, those directories too.
 */
function readTargets(scope: GuardScope, cwd: string, tool: string, input: Record<string, unknown>): string[] {
  if (tool === 'Read') {
    return typeof input.file_path === 'string' ? [realPathOf(toolPath(scope, cwd, input.file_path))] : [];
  }
  const given = typeof input.path === 'string' && input.path.trim() !== '';
  const base = given ? toolPath(scope, cwd, input.path as string) : resolve(cwd);
  const targets = [realPathOf(base)];
  if (tool === 'Glob' && typeof input.pattern === 'string') {
    const fixed = fixedPrefix(expandHome(scope, input.pattern.trim()));
    if (fixed !== '') targets.push(realPathOf(resolve(base, fixed)));
  }
  return targets;
}

function judgeRead(tool: string, targets: string[], root: Roots): Verdict {
  // Glob and Grep descend: a root above the work root or the projects directory would reach into them.
  const descends = tool !== 'Read';
  for (const target of targets) {
    if (within(target, root.work) && !within(target, root.clone)) {
      return refuse(`${tool} is in another attempt's clone, which is refused`);
    }
    if (descends && within(root.work, target) && target !== root.work) {
      return refuse(`${tool} would search other attempts' clones, which is refused`);
    }
    if (within(target, root.projects) && !within(target, root.ownProject)) {
      return refuse(`${tool} is in another session's Claude project directory, which is refused`);
    }
    if (descends && within(root.projects, target) && target !== root.projects) {
      return refuse(`${tool} would search other sessions' Claude project directories, which is refused`);
    }
  }
  return ALLOW;
}

/**
 * The leading directories of a glob pattern before its first wildcard. A pattern without one names a file, and the
 * CLI searches its directory for it.
 */
function fixedPrefix(pattern: string): string {
  const parts = pattern.split('/');
  const wild = parts.findIndex((part) => GLOB_CHARS.test(part));
  const fixed = wild < 0 ? parts.slice(0, -1) : parts.slice(0, wild);
  return fixed.length === 1 && fixed[0] === '' && isAbsolute(pattern) ? '/' : fixed.join('/');
}

/** A tool path as 2.1.285 resolves it: trimmed, ~ expanded, relative to the current directory, NFC-normalized. */
function toolPath(scope: GuardScope, cwd: string, path: string): string {
  return resolve(cwd, expandHome(scope, path.trim())).normalize('NFC');
}

function expandHome(scope: GuardScope, path: string): string {
  if (path === '~') return scope.home;
  return path.startsWith('~/') ? join(scope.home, path.slice(2)) : path;
}

function within(path: string, root: string): boolean {
  return path === root || path.startsWith(root.endsWith(sep) ? root : `${root}${sep}`);
}

function refuse(reason: string): Verdict {
  return { allow: false, reason };
}
```

```ts
// Paths the Claude adapter shares between the guard, the sandbox settings and the transcripts (design 7.6): real
// paths, and the project directory Claude Code 2.1.285 keeps an attempt's transcripts and oversized tool output in.
import { lstatSync, readlinkSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs';
import { basename, dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path';

/** Past this length the CLI cuts the slug and appends a hash, which the runner does not reproduce. */
export const MAX_CLAUDE_PROJECT_SLUG = 200;

/** Symbolic links followed by hand before a path counts as a loop. */
const MAX_LINKS = 40;

/**
 * The real path of `path`, also when it does not exist yet: a missing path is its nearest existing parent's real path
 * plus the rest, and a dangling symlink is followed to where a write through it would land. On a case-insensitive
 * volume the existing part comes back in its on-disk case.
 */
export function realPathOf(path: string): string {
  return resolveReal(resolve(path), 0);
}

function resolveReal(path: string, links: number): string {
  if (links > MAX_LINKS) throw new Error(`too many symbolic links at ${path}`);
  try {
    return realpathSync.native(path);
  } catch {
    // Missing, a dangling link or a loop: walk it by hand below.
  }
  let link: string | null = null;
  try {
    if (lstatSync(path).isSymbolicLink()) link = readlinkSync(path);
  } catch {
    // The path itself is missing; its parent decides.
  }
  if (link !== null) return resolveReal(resolve(dirname(path), link), links + 1);
  const parent = dirname(path);
  if (parent === path) return path;
  return join(resolveReal(parent, links), basename(path));
}

/**
 * The name of a clone's project directory, as 2.1.285 forms it: the real path of its working directory with every
 * character other than A-Z, a-z and 0-9 replaced by '-'. Slugs longer than 200 characters are refused.
 */
export function claudeProjectSlug(clone: string): string {
  const real = realPathOf(clone);
  const slug = real.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, '-');
  if (slug.length > MAX_CLAUDE_PROJECT_SLUG) {
    throw new Error(
      `the clone path ${real} gives a Claude project name of ${slug.length} characters; ` +
        `Claude Code shortens names over ${MAX_CLAUDE_PROJECT_SLUG} with a hash, so the runner refuses the clone`,
    );
  }
  return slug;
}

/** <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/projects/<slug>: the attempt's transcripts and the tool output the CLI persists. */
export function claudeProjectDir(claudeHome: string, clone: string): string {
  return join(claudeHome, 'projects', claudeProjectSlug(clone));
}
```

### Task 7: Claude permission rules and sandbox settings

Section 7.6's denied paths, which M2b's `deniedReadPaths` and `deniedWritePaths` give, rendered for Claude Code 2.1.285 (design 7.6, 8.2, X-29). `claudePermissionRules` gives deny rules in the absolute `//path` form for the in-process tools, the Bash push rules (`Bash(git push:*)`, `gh`, `glab`, `security`, …) and allow rules for `mcp__agflow`, the web tools with `webTools`, and Read and Edit of the attempt's tmpDir. Read rules name only 7.6's sensitive parts of `~/.agflow/runner` (`CLAUDE_RUNNER_READ_PARTS`) and never the work root, so the CLI can still read oversized tool output in the attempt's project directory. `claudeSandboxSettings` gives `denyRead` (the runner tree and each `work/*/*` attempt), `allowRead` (the clone and its project directory), `allowWrite` (the tmpDir), `denyWrite` (`/tmp/claude`, `/private/tmp/claude`, `~/.npm/_logs`) and the network allowlist with `strictAllowlist`. Rendering fails closed on a root path with a glob character and on a deny that would cover the clone or the tmpDir. Sandbox `denyRead` names each attempt through `join(paths.work, '*', '*')`, leaving the work root and project parents readable for Bun's package-script resolution. `allowRead` remains the current clone and its Claude project directory. Plain-path validation runs before the generated glob is added; caller-supplied pattern characters remain forbidden. Permission Read/Edit deny rules still do not name the work root. Claude Code 2.1.285 honours the generated `denyRead` glob through `--settings`: `bun run` succeeds, while reads of another attempt in the same project or another project fail, including reads inside an executing script.

```ts
// Section 7.6's denied paths rendered for Claude Code 2.1.285 (design 7.6, 8.2, X-29): permission rules in the
// absolute //path form for the in-process tools, and the sandbox's filesystem and network settings for Bash. Every
// path comes from the given home and runner paths, never from the runner's own environment.
import { isAbsolute, join } from 'node:path';
import type { Vendor } from '@agflow/core';
import type { SandboxSettings } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';
import type { RunnerPaths } from '../../paths';
import { type DeniedPath, deniedReadPaths, deniedWritePaths, type PermissionProfile } from '../../profile';
import { claudeProjectDir } from './paths';

/**
 * The parts of ~/.agflow/runner that Read rules name (7.6). The whole tree cannot be named: a Read rule has no
 * allowRead carve-out, and Claude Code tells the model to read oversized tool output in the attempt's project
 * directory under homes/claude/projects/.
 */
export const CLAUDE_RUNNER_READ_PARTS: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([
  'runner.*',
  'logs/**',
  'git/**',
  'prep/**',
  'forensics/**',
  'homes/codex/**',
  'homes/codex-user/**',
  'homes/claude/.claude.json',
  'homes/claude/backups/**',
  'homes/claude/shell-snapshots/**',
]);

/** The same Claude-home parts, named under a Claude home that runner.json puts outside the runner tree. */
const CLAUDE_HOME_READ_PARTS = ['.claude.json', 'backups/**', 'shell-snapshots/**'];

/**
 * Bash deny rules for the commands that reach the git host or credentials. The `:*` form also matches the bare
 * command. The guard refuses these and more, with real parsing; the rules are the CLI's own second line.
 */
export const CLAUDE_PUSH_DENY_RULES: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([
  'Bash(git push:*)',
  'Bash(git credential:*)',
  'Bash(gh:*)',
  'Bash(glab:*)',
  'Bash(security:*)',
]);

const BRIDGE_TOOLS = 'mcp__agflow';
const WEB_TOOLS = ['WebFetch', 'WebSearch'];

/** The sandbox runtime always lets commands write these unless they are denied by name (7.6, X-29). */
const SHARED_TMP = ['/tmp/claude', '/private/tmp/claude'];

// Rule contents and sandbox paths are glob patterns: a path holding one of these would match something else, or
// break the rule's parentheses, and a deny that silently matches nothing must not happen.
const PATTERN_CHARS = /[*?[\]{}()\\]/;

export interface ClaudeRulesInput {
  /** The agent's HOME (the owner's), given rather than read from the process. */
  home: string;
  /** From runnerPaths(AGFLOW_HOME). */
  paths: Pick<RunnerPaths, 'runner' | 'vaults' | 'work'>;
  /** vendorHomes(config, paths); the Claude home is CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. */
  vendorHomes: Record<Vendor, string>;
  profile: PermissionProfile;
  /** The attempt's clone. */
  clone: string;
  /** CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR. */
  tmpDir: string;
}

export interface ClaudePermissionRules {
  allow: string[];
  deny: string[];
}

/**
 * settings.permissions: the bridge (and the web tools with webTools) and the temporary directory allowed, 7.6's reads
 * and writes denied.
 */
export function claudePermissionRules(input: ClaudeRulesInput): ClaudePermissionRules {
  const { readable, writable } = deniedPaths(input);
  const claudeHome = input.vendorHomes.claude;
  const reads = new Set<string>();
  for (const denied of readable) {
    if (denied.path === input.paths.runner) {
      for (const part of CLAUDE_RUNNER_READ_PARTS) reads.add(rule('Read', join(input.paths.runner, part)));
    } else if (denied.path !== claudeHome) {
      reads.add(pathRule('Read', denied));
    }
  }
  // Wherever the Claude home lies, only its sensitive parts are named, so the project directory stays readable.
  for (const part of CLAUDE_HOME_READ_PARTS) reads.add(rule('Read', join(claudeHome, part)));
  // Edit rules cover Write and NotebookEdit too; 2.1.285 never matches path patterns in Write(...) rules.
  const edits = new Set(writable.map((denied) => pathRule('Edit', denied)));
  return {
    allow: [
      BRIDGE_TOOLS,
      ...(input.profile.webTools ? WEB_TOOLS : []),
      // Under acceptEdits and permissionPrompts 'none', 2.1.285 refuses in-process tools outside the cwd, so the
      // temporary directory the guard and the sandbox give the agent needs allow rules of its own. Not
      // additionalDirectories: --add-dir would also load skills and commands from there.
      rule('Read', join(input.tmpDir, '**')),
      rule('Edit', join(input.tmpDir, '**')),
    ],
    deny: [...reads, ...edits, ...CLAUDE_PUSH_DENY_RULES],
  };
}

/**
 * The top-level sandbox option. denyRead holds 7.6's list plus a two-level glob under work (each clone), with allowRead
 * for the clone and the attempt's project directory. Leaving the clone's parents readable lets Bun resolve package
 * scripts; 2.1.285 honours this generated glob through --settings. Writes go only to the clone (the CLI adds its cwd) and
 * the temporary directory. The CLI copies the Edit deny rules into denyWrite itself.
 */
export function claudeSandboxSettings(input: ClaudeRulesInput): SandboxSettings {
  const { readable } = deniedPaths(input);
  return {
    enabled: true,
    failIfUnavailable: true,
    allowUnsandboxedCommands: false,
    network: { allowedDomains: [...input.profile.network.allowedDomains], strictAllowlist: true },
    filesystem: {
      denyRead: [...new Set([...readable.map((denied) => denied.path), join(input.paths.work, '*', '*')])],
      allowRead: [input.clone, claudeProjectDir(input.vendorHomes.claude, input.clone)],
      allowWrite: [input.tmpDir],
      denyWrite: [...SHARED_TMP, join(input.home, '.npm', '_logs')],
    },
  };
}

/**
 * 7.6's lists for this input, after checking that every path is plain and that no denial covers the attempt's own
 * files: deny rules cannot be re-allowed, and Edit denials become sandbox denyWrite paths. (profile.ts already
 * refuses denials that cover the work root.)
 */
function deniedPaths(input: ClaudeRulesInput): { readable: DeniedPath[]; writable: DeniedPath[] } {
  const roots = [input.home, input.paths.runner, input.paths.vaults, input.paths.work, input.clone, input.tmpDir];
  for (const path of [...roots, ...Object.values(input.vendorHomes)]) plainPath(path);
  const readable = deniedReadPaths(input);
  const writable = deniedWritePaths(input);
  for (const denied of [...readable, ...writable]) {
    for (const own of [input.clone, input.tmpDir]) {
      if (own === denied.path || own.startsWith(`${denied.path}/`)) {
        throw new Error(`the denied path ${denied.path} would cover the attempt's ${own}`);
      }
    }
  }
  return { readable, writable };
}

function pathRule(tool: 'Read' | 'Edit', denied: DeniedPath): string {
  return rule(tool, denied.tree ? join(denied.path, '**') : denied.path);
}

/** `Tool(//abs)`: a leading // makes the pattern an absolute filesystem path. */
function rule(tool: 'Read' | 'Edit', path: string): string {
  return `${tool}(/${path})`;
}

function plainPath(path: string): void {
  if (!isAbsolute(path)) throw new Error(`a Claude permission path must be absolute, not ${path}`);
  if (PATTERN_CHARS.test(path)) {
    throw new Error(`the path ${path} holds characters Claude Code reads as a pattern; move it or AGFLOW_HOME`);
  }
}
```
