// Boundary 1 and the keychain with the real claude (design 5, 15, 7.6), gated by AGFLOW_SANDBOX_CHECKS=1 (X-20),
// macOS only. The model runs the probe scripts from the clone through real sandboxed Bash calls, so the guard never
// pre-empts the sandbox, and the same scripts run outside for comparison. Claude's sandbox proxy chains through the
// CLI's HTTPS_PROXY, so the network checks give the CLI a test proxy that tunnels only to the allowed registry and
// refuses and records every other target; the model still comes only from the scripted server.
import { afterAll, afterEach, describe, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { claudePin } from '../../src/adapters/claude/pin';
import { vendorPlatform } from '../../src/vendor/pins';
import { cleanupClaudeSmokes, smokeDescribe, startClaudeSmoke } from '../claude-real/harness';
import {
  type CheckRow,
  CheckTable,
  formatChecks,
  mismatches,
  outsideEnv,
  type ProbeResults,
  probeCommand,
  runAsAgent,
  runOutside,
  SANDBOX_GIT_HOST,
  SANDBOX_REGISTRY,
  sandboxGate,
  throwawayKeychain,
} from './checks';

// A cold start of the CLI, its sandbox, the bridge and the brief hook, plus probes that wait out unreachable hosts.
setDefaultTimeout(300_000);

const table = new CheckTable('Sandbox checks: network and keychain');
const keychains = new Set<() => void>();

afterEach(async () => {
  // The throwaway keychain goes even when a test failed before its own cleanup ran.
  for (const remove of [...keychains]) remove();
  keychains.clear();
  await cleanupClaudeSmokes();
});
afterAll(() => table.print());

const gate = sandboxGate();

/** The only target the network checks' test proxy tunnels to the real host. */
const EGRESS = [`${SANDBOX_REGISTRY}:443`];

describe('sandboxGate', () => {
  test('without AGFLOW_SANDBOX_CHECKS=1 the checks are skipped with the reason', () => {
    const result = sandboxGate({ env: { AGFLOW_SMOKE: '1' }, platform: 'darwin' });
    expect(result).toEqual({ run: false, bin: null, reason: 'AGFLOW_SANDBOX_CHECKS=1 not set' });
    expect(sandboxGate({ env: { AGFLOW_SMOKE: '1', AGFLOW_SANDBOX_CHECKS: '1' }, platform: 'linux' }).reason).toBe(
      'the sandbox checks need macOS, not linux',
    );
  });

  test('without the pinned binary the checks are skipped with the reason', () => {
    const missing = '/nonexistent/agflow-claude';
    const env = { AGFLOW_SMOKE: '1', AGFLOW_SANDBOX_CHECKS: '1', AGFLOW_CLAUDE_BIN: missing };
    const result = sandboxGate({ env, home: '/nonexistent', platform: 'darwin' });
    expect(result.run).toBe(false);
    // On a platform without a pin (CI's Linux) the gate stops there.
    if (claudePin(vendorPlatform()) === null) {
      expect(result.reason).toBe(`agflow pins no claude for ${vendorPlatform()}`);
    } else {
      expect(result.reason).toContain(`AGFLOW_CLAUDE_BIN ${missing} is missing`);
      expect(result.reason).toContain('bun run vendor:install');
    }
  });

  test('the check table lists each check with its expected and observed result', () => {
    const text = formatChecks('Checks', [
      { check: 'hub over HTTP', expected: 'blocked', observed: 'blocked', skipped: null },
      { check: 'registry over HTTPS', expected: 'reached', observed: 'blocked', skipped: null },
      { check: 'git host over SSH', expected: 'blocked', observed: '', skipped: 'unreachable outside' },
    ]);
    expect(text.split('\n')).toEqual([
      'Checks',
      '  check                expected  observed',
      '  hub over HTTP        blocked   blocked',
      '  registry over HTTPS  reached   blocked  MISMATCH',
      '  git host over SSH    blocked   skipped: unreachable outside',
    ]);
  });
});

smokeDescribe(gate, 'sandbox checks: network', () => {
  test('a sandboxed command reaches neither the hub URL nor the git host, over HTTPS or SSH', async () => {
    const smoke = await startClaudeSmoke({ bin: gate.bin ?? undefined, egress: EGRESS });
    const hubUrl = smoke.launch().env.AGFLOW_HUB_URL;
    if (!hubUrl) throw new Error('the agent environment has no AGFLOW_HUB_URL');
    // The sandbox has no DNS, so the direct probes use the address resolved outside.
    const address = await resolveHost(SANDBOX_GIT_HOST);
    const gitHost = `https://${SANDBOX_GIT_HOST}/`;
    // A refusing proxy answers plain HTTP itself, so the hub counts as reached only when it saw the probe's own path.
    const hubPath = (side: string, route: string) => `/agflow-probe/${side}/${route}`;
    const probes = (side: string): Probe[] => [
      ['hub over HTTP through the sandbox proxy', 'http', `${hubUrl}${hubPath(side, 'proxy')}`, 'env', '-'],
      ['hub over HTTP directly', 'http', `${hubUrl}${hubPath(side, 'direct')}`, 'direct', '-'],
      ...(address === null
        ? []
        : ([
            ['git host over HTTPS through the sandbox proxy', 'http', gitHost, 'env', '-'],
            ['git host over HTTPS directly', 'http', gitHost, 'direct', `${SANDBOX_GIT_HOST}:443:${address}`],
            ['git host over SSH through the sandbox proxy', 'ssh', SANDBOX_GIT_HOST, 'env', '-'],
            ['git host over SSH directly', 'ssh', address, 'direct', '-'],
          ] satisfies Probe[])),
    ];
    const outside = await runOutside('net.sh', probes('outside').flat(), outsideEnv(smoke));
    const inside = await runAsAgent(smoke, [probeCommand('net.sh', probes('inside').flat())]);
    const hubSaw = (path: string) => smoke.hubRequests.some((request) => request.path === path);
    const rows: CheckRow[] = [];
    for (const [label, , target] of probes('outside')) {
      const route = target.startsWith(hubUrl) ? target.slice(target.lastIndexOf('/') + 1) : null;
      const reached = (side: string, results: ProbeResults) => {
        if (route === null) return results.get(label)?.result ?? 'no answer';
        return hubSaw(hubPath(side, route)) ? 'reached' : 'blocked';
      };
      const before = reached('outside', outside);
      if (route !== null && before !== 'reached') throw new Error(`the hub is unreachable outside the sandbox too`);
      rows.push({
        check: `sandboxed ${label}`,
        expected: 'blocked',
        observed: reached('inside', inside),
        skipped: before === 'reached' ? null : `unreachable outside: ${outside.get(label)?.detail ?? 'no answer'}`,
      });
    }
    if (address === null) {
      rows.push({
        check: `sandboxed ${SANDBOX_GIT_HOST}`,
        expected: 'blocked',
        observed: '',
        skipped: `${SANDBOX_GIT_HOST} does not resolve outside: offline`,
      });
    }
    expect(mismatches(table.add(...rows))).toEqual([]);
    expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
  });

  test(`an allowed registry (${SANDBOX_REGISTRY}) is reachable inside, through the HTTP and SOCKS proxy`, async () => {
    const smoke = await startClaudeSmoke({ bin: gate.bin ?? undefined, egress: EGRESS });
    const url = `https://${SANDBOX_REGISTRY}/`;
    // The SOCKS route is the git host's SSH probe's: reaching the registry shows that route works, so the git host's
    // refusal there comes from the allow list.
    const viaProxy: Probe = ['registry over HTTPS through the sandbox proxy', 'http', url, 'env', '-'];
    const viaSocks: Probe = ['registry over HTTPS through the sandbox SOCKS proxy', 'http', url, 'socks', '-'];
    const probes = [viaProxy, viaSocks];
    // Outside, without proxies, both routes are the same request.
    const outside = (await runOutside('net.sh', viaProxy, outsideEnv(smoke))).get(viaProxy[0]);
    if (outside?.result !== 'reached') {
      table.add(
        ...probes.map(([label]) => ({
          check: `sandboxed ${label}`,
          expected: 'reached',
          observed: '',
          skipped: `unreachable outside: ${outside?.detail ?? 'no answer'}`,
        })),
      );
      return;
    }
    const inside = await runAsAgent(smoke, [probeCommand('net.sh', probes.flat())]);
    const rows = probes.map(([label]) => ({
      check: `sandboxed ${label}`,
      expected: 'reached',
      observed: inside.get(label)?.result ?? 'no answer',
    }));
    expect(mismatches(table.add(...rows))).toEqual([]);
    expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
  });
});

smokeDescribe(gate, 'sandbox checks: keychain', () => {
  test('a throwaway generic-password item is readable outside the sandbox and not inside', async () => {
    const smoke = await startClaudeSmoke({ bin: gate.bin ?? undefined });
    // The deny list names <HOME>/Library/Keychains for the agent's HOME, so the item's keychain lies there. The CLI
    // never gets the owner's HOME in a test (it writes ~/.claude and caches into it), and the owner's login keychain
    // is never touched: a throwaway keychain file is read in-process, like the login keychain.
    const directory = join(smoke.home, 'Library', 'Keychains');
    mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true });
    const item = throwawayKeychain(join(directory, 'agflow-probe.keychain-db'), smoke.home);
    keychains.add(item.remove);
    try {
      const args = ['keychain item', item.path, item.service, item.account];
      const outside = (await runOutside('keychain.sh', args, outsideEnv(smoke))).get('keychain item');
      const before = table.add({
        check: 'keychain item read outside the sandbox',
        expected: 'read',
        observed: outside?.detail === item.secret ? 'read' : (outside?.result ?? 'no answer'),
      });
      const inside = (await runAsAgent(smoke, [probeCommand('keychain.sh', args)])).get('keychain item');
      // Read outside again: a refusal inside counts only while the item was readable all along.
      const again = (await runOutside('keychain.sh', args, outsideEnv(smoke))).get('keychain item');
      const after = table.add(
        { check: 'sandboxed keychain item read', expected: 'refused', observed: inside?.result ?? 'no answer' },
        {
          check: 'keychain item read outside the sandbox afterwards',
          expected: 'read',
          observed: again?.detail === item.secret ? 'read' : (again?.result ?? 'no answer'),
        },
      );
      expect(mismatches([...before, ...after])).toEqual([]);
      expect(inside?.detail).not.toContain(item.secret);
      expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
    } finally {
      item.remove();
      keychains.delete(item.remove);
    }
    expect(existsSync(item.path)).toBe(false);
  });
});

/** A net.sh probe: its label, kind, target, way (env, socks or direct) and curl's --resolve entry, or '-'. */
type Probe = [label: string, kind: 'http' | 'ssh', target: string, via: 'env' | 'socks' | 'direct', resolve: string];

/** The host's IPv4 address, or null when it does not resolve: offline. */
async function resolveHost(host: string): Promise<string | null> {
  try {
    return (await Bun.dns.lookup(host, { family: 4 }))[0]?.address ?? null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

#!/bin/sh
# A keychain probe of the sandbox checks (design 5, keychain): looks a generic-password item up in a keychain file
# and prints `PROBE <label>: read <secret>` or `PROBE <label>: refused <error>`.
# Usage: keychain.sh <label> <keychain> <service> <account>

out=$(security find-generic-password -s "$3" -a "$4" -w "$2" 2>&1)
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
  printf 'PROBE %s: read %s\n' "$1" "$out"
else
  printf 'PROBE %s: refused %s\n' "$1" "$(printf '%s' "$out" | tr '\r\n' '  ' | cut -c1-240)"
fi

```bash
#!/bin/sh
# A network probe of the sandbox checks (design 5, boundary 1). Each probe is five words,
#   <label> http <url> env|socks|direct <host>:<port>:<address>|-
#   <label> ssh <host> env|direct -
# and prints `PROBE <label>: reached|blocked <detail>`. A plain HTTP url that got a response prints `answered`
# instead: a refusing proxy answers those itself, so only the target can tell whether it was reached.
# "env" goes the way the environment's proxies send it, with NO_PROXY cleared so loopback goes there too (inside the
# sandbox: Claude's sandbox proxy); "socks" goes through the SOCKS side of the proxy ALL_PROXY names, with its
# credentials; "direct" bypasses every proxy. The sandbox has no DNS, so a direct probe names the address (curl's
# --resolve, or the address as the host). The SSH probe uses no configuration, key or agent: it only checks that a key
# exchange with the host happened.

result() {
  printf 'PROBE %s: %s %s\n' "$1" "$2" "$(printf '%s' "$3" | tr '\r\n' '  ' | cut -c1-240)"
}

http_probe() {
  label=$1 url=$2 via=$3 resolve=$4
  set -- -sS -o /dev/null -m 10 -w '%{http_code}'
  if [ "$resolve" != - ]; then set -- "$@" --resolve "$resolve"; fi
  if [ "$via" = direct ]; then
    out=$(curl --noproxy '*' "$@" "$url" 2>&1)
  elif [ "$via" = socks ]; then
    out=$(curl -x "$(socks_proxy)" "$@" "$url" 2>&1)
  else
    out=$(NO_PROXY= no_proxy= curl "$@" "$url" 2>&1)
  fi
  status=$?
  if [ $status -ne 0 ]; then
    result "$label" blocked "$out"
  elif [ "${url#https://}" != "$url" ]; then
    result "$label" reached "HTTP $out"
  else
    result "$label" answered "HTTP $out"
  fi
}

# The SOCKS URL of the proxy ALL_PROXY names, with its credentials: the sandbox's proxy speaks SOCKS on the same port
# and lets only clients that authenticate reach its allow list.
socks_proxy() {
  proxy=${ALL_PROXY#*://}
  printf 'socks5h://%s' "${proxy%/}"
}

ssh_probe() {
  label=$1 host=$2 via=$3
  if [ "$via" = env ] && [ -n "${ALL_PROXY:-}" ]; then
    socks_ssh_probe "$label" "$host"
    return
  fi
  out=$(ssh -v -F /dev/null -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o IdentityAgent=none -o IdentitiesOnly=yes \
    -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -o PasswordAuthentication=no -o KbdInteractiveAuthentication=no \
    -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -p 22 "git@$host" true 2>&1 </dev/null)
  case $out in
    *'Server host key:'*) result "$label" reached "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep 'Server host key:')" ;;
    *) result "$label" blocked "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -v '^debug' | tail -n 2)" ;;
  esac
}

# Port 22 through the sandbox's SOCKS proxy, authenticated as an agent could with ALL_PROXY's credentials. The
# sandbox's own GIT_SSH_COMMAND (nc -X 5) offers no authentication, and an unauthenticated client gets an SSH banner
# of `policy_refusal` whatever the allow list says, so that banner never counts as blocked.
socks_ssh_probe() {
  label=$1 host=$2
  out=$(curl -v -sS -m 10 -x "$(socks_proxy)" "telnet://$host:22" 2>&1 </dev/null)
  case $out in
    *'SSH-2.0-policy_refusal'*) result "$label" unauthenticated "the proxy took the probe as unauthenticated" ;;
    *"Can't complete SOCKS5 connection to $host. (2)"*) result "$label" blocked "SOCKS5 refused by the ruleset" ;;
    *'SSH-2.0-'* | *'SOCKS5 request granted'*)
      result "$label" reached "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E 'SSH-2.0-|SOCKS5 request granted' | head -n 1)" ;;
    *) result "$label" unknown "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -n 2)" ;;
  esac
}

while [ $# -ge 5 ]; do
  case $2 in
    http) http_probe "$1" "$3" "$4" "$5" ;;
    ssh) ssh_probe "$1" "$3" "$4" ;;
    *) result "$1" unknown "no probe kind $2" ;;
  esac
  shift 5
done
```

These checks skip unless `AGFLOW_SMOKE=1`, `AGFLOW_SANDBOX_CHECKS=1`, macOS and a located pin (export `AGFLOW_CLAUDE_BIN`, see the conventions). The real claude talks only to the scripted server on 127.0.0.1, with the fake key and scratch homes; no test sends a prompt to a real model. Each test prints its table of expected and observed results. They pass at once: Tasks 7 and 8 set the sandbox up. The network checks reach github.com and registry.npmjs.org for their controls; rows for a host that the same probe cannot reach outside are skipped with the reason. The SSH probe authenticates to the sandbox's SOCKS proxy with `ALL_PROXY`'s credentials, as an agent could: 2.1.285's own `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` (`nc -X 5`, no authentication) gets an `SSH-2.0-policy_refused` banner for any host, so a banner never counts, only a real key exchange. The hub counts as reached only when the tap recorded the probe's own path, because a proxy answers refused plain HTTP itself.

### Task 28: Sandbox checks: write confinement, TMPDIR and the shared directories

Local checks of boundary 2 for sandboxed commands (design 5, 7.6, 15; X-29). A write probe runs outside first, then inside: writes to `HOME`, the base checkout, another attempt's `/tmp/agf/<id>` and the Claude home's empty directory (Task 8's `ZDOTDIR`, and the bridge's and hook's working directory) are refused, and writes to the clone and the attempt's own tmpDir succeed. The commands' `TMPDIR` is under `/tmp/agf/<id>/`, and `mktemp` works there. Writes to `~/.npm/_logs`, `/tmp/claude` and `/private/tmp/claude` are refused on 2.1.285, which settles `TMP_CLAUDE_DENYWRITE_ENFORCED = true`: only the constant's comment changes, and the check fails whenever the constant disagrees with the sandbox or a row could not be checked, and confirms that preflight lists `'/tmp/claude'` exactly when the constant is false. Check write confinement, TMPDIR and the shared directories in `writes.test.ts`. The Bun package-script and sibling-clone read regression belongs to Task 29 because it uses `runAgentSteps`, which Task 29 introduces. Task 28 must load and typecheck without that helper.

```bash
#!/bin/sh
# A write probe of the sandbox checks (design 5, boundary 2). It prints the commands' temporary directory as
# `PROBE TMPDIR: is <value>` and makes a file there with mktemp (named after TMPDIR: macOS's bare mktemp uses the
# per-user /var/folders directory, which the sandbox refuses). Then, for each label and directory, it makes the
# directory if it is missing and a file in it. Each write prints `PROBE <label>: written <file>` or
# `PROBE <label>: refused <error>`.
# Usage: writes.sh [<label> <directory> ...]

refused() {
  printf 'PROBE %s: refused %s\n' "$1" "$(printf '%s' "$2" | tr '\r\n' '  ' | cut -c1-240)"
}

printf 'PROBE TMPDIR: is %s\n' "${TMPDIR:-unset}"
if out=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agflow-probe.XXXXXX" 2>&1); then
  printf 'PROBE mktemp: written %s\n' "$out"
else
  refused mktemp "$out"
fi
while [ $# -ge 2 ]; do
  file="$2/agflow-write-probe-$$"
  if out=$( { mkdir -p "$2" && printf 'agflow write probe\n' >"$file"; } 2>&1 ); then
    printf 'PROBE %s: written %s\n' "$1" "$file"
  else
    refused "$1" "$out"
  fi
  shift 2
done

```ts
// Boundary 2 for sandboxed commands with the real claude (design 5, 7.6, 15, 8.1; X-29), gated by
// AGFLOW_SANDBOX_CHECKS=1 (X-20), macOS only. The model runs the write probe from the clone through a real sandboxed
// Bash call; the same probe runs outside first, so a refusal inside counts only where the test process can write.
// The Claude home's empty directory is among the refused targets: zsh reads its startup files there outside the sandbox
// (ZDOTDIR), and the bridge and the brief hook start in it (options.ts, claudeEmptyDir).
// What the sandbox does with /tmp/claude is what TMP_CLAUDE_DENYWRITE_ENFORCED records for the pin, and preflight's
// weakened list follows the constant.
import { afterAll, afterEach, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, rmdirSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { ensureClaudeEmptyDir } from '../../src/adapters/claude/options';
import { CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION, TMP_CLAUDE_DENYWRITE_ENFORCED } from '../../src/adapters/claude/pin';
import { makeAttemptTmpDir } from '../../src/paths';
import { type ClaudeSmoke, cleanupClaudeSmokes, smokeDescribe, startClaudeSmoke } from '../claude-real/harness';
import {
  type CheckRow,
  CheckTable,
  mismatches,
  outsideEnv,
  type ProbeResults,
  probeCommand,
  runAsAgent,
  runOutside,
  sandboxGate,
} from './checks';

// A cold start of the CLI, its sandbox, the bridge and the brief hook, on a machine other suites may load.
setDefaultTimeout(300_000);

const table = new CheckTable(`Sandbox checks: writes (claude ${CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION})`);
const cleanups = new Set<() => void>();

afterEach(async () => {
  for (const cleanup of [...cleanups]) cleanup();
  cleanups.clear();
  await cleanupClaudeSmokes();
});
afterAll(() => table.print());

const gate = sandboxGate();

/** The shared directories the sandbox runtime lets every command write unless they are denied by name (7.6). */
const SHARED_TMP = ['/tmp/claude', '/private/tmp/claude'];

type Expected = 'written' | 'refused';

interface WriteProbe {
  outside: ProbeResults;
  inside: ProbeResults;
  /** One row per target: refused or written inside, skipped where the test process cannot write either. */
  rows: CheckRow[];
}

/**
 * Runs the write probe outside and then as the agent, for each target, and removes every file either run wrote. A
 * shared directory the outside run had to make goes again too.
 */
async function probeWrites(
  smoke: ClaudeSmoke,
  targets: [label: string, directory: string, expected: Expected][],
): Promise<WriteProbe> {
  for (const path of SHARED_TMP.filter((path) => !existsSync(path))) {
    cleanups.add(() => {
      if (existsSync(path) && readdirSync(path).length === 0) rmdirSync(path);
    });
  }
  const args = targets.flatMap(([label, directory]) => [label, directory]);
  const outside = await runOutside('writes.sh', args, outsideEnv(smoke));
  let inside: ProbeResults = new Map();
  try {
    inside = await runAsAgent(smoke, [probeCommand('writes.sh', args)]);
  } finally {
    for (const results of [outside, inside]) {
      for (const { result, detail } of results.values()) if (result === 'written') rmSync(detail, { force: true });
    }
  }
  const rows = targets.map(([label, , expected]): CheckRow => {
    const before = outside.get(label);
    return {
      check: `sandboxed write to ${label}`,
      expected,
      observed: inside.get(label)?.result ?? 'no answer',
      skipped: before?.result === 'written' ? null : `not writable outside either: ${before?.detail ?? 'no answer'}`,
    };
  });
  return { outside, inside, rows };
}

smokeDescribe(gate, 'sandbox checks: writes', () => {
  test(
    "writes fail in HOME, the base checkout, the Claude home's empty directory and another attempt's tmpDir, " +
      'and work in the clone and its own tmpDir',
    async () => {
      const smoke = await startClaudeSmoke({ bin: gate.bin ?? undefined });
      const other = makeAttemptTmpDir();
      cleanups.add(() => rmSync(other, { recursive: true, force: true }));
      // The runner makes it before every launch; the outside run comes before the first.
      const empty = ensureClaudeEmptyDir(smoke.claudeHome);
      const { rows } = await probeWrites(smoke, [
        ['HOME', smoke.home, 'refused'],
        ['the base checkout', smoke.baseCheckout, 'refused'],
        ["the Claude home's empty directory (ZDOTDIR, the bridge's and hook's cwd)", empty, 'refused'],
        [`another attempt's ${other}`, other, 'refused'],
        ['the clone', smoke.clone, 'written'],
        [`the attempt's own ${smoke.tmpDir}`, smoke.tmpDir, 'written'],
      ]);
      expect(mismatches(table.add(...rows))).toEqual([]);
      expect(rows.filter((row) => row.skipped)).toEqual([]);
      expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
    },
  );

  test("the commands' TMPDIR is under the attempt's /tmp/agf/<id>/, and mktemp works there", async () => {
    const smoke = await startClaudeSmoke({ bin: gate.bin ?? undefined });
    const { inside } = await probeWrites(smoke, []);
    const under = (path: string | undefined) => path?.startsWith(`${smoke.tmpDir}/`) ?? false;
    const expected = `under ${smoke.tmpDir}/`;
    const value = inside.get('TMPDIR')?.detail;
    const temporary = inside.get('mktemp');
    const made = temporary?.result === 'written' && under(temporary.detail);
    const rows = table.add(
      { check: "the commands' TMPDIR", expected, observed: under(value) ? expected : (value ?? 'no answer') },
      {
        check: 'a sandboxed mktemp',
        expected: `written ${expected}`,
        observed: made ? `written ${expected}` : `${temporary?.result ?? 'no answer'} ${temporary?.detail ?? ''}`,
      },
    );
    expect(mismatches(rows)).toEqual([]);
    expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('writes to ~/.npm/_logs are refused, and /tmp/claude does what TMP_CLAUDE_DENYWRITE_ENFORCED says', async () => {
    const smoke = await startClaudeSmoke({ bin: gate.bin ?? undefined });
    // npm made its log directory already, as it has in the owner's home.
    const npmLogs = join(smoke.home, '.npm', '_logs');
    mkdirSync(npmLogs, { recursive: true });
    const shared: Expected = TMP_CLAUDE_DENYWRITE_ENFORCED ? 'refused' : 'written';
    const { rows } = await probeWrites(smoke, [
      ['~/.npm/_logs', npmLogs, 'refused'],
      ...SHARED_TMP.map((path): [string, string, Expected] => [path, path, shared]),
    ]);
    const { weakened } = await smoke.adapter.preflight();
    const listed = TMP_CLAUDE_DENYWRITE_ENFORCED ? 'not listed' : 'listed';
    rows.push({
      check: "preflight's weakened list names '/tmp/claude'",
      expected: listed,
      observed: weakened.includes('/tmp/claude') ? 'listed' : 'not listed',
    });
    const wrong = mismatches(table.add(...rows));
    expect(
      rows.filter((row) => row.skipped),
      'the shared directories could not be checked from this account, so TMP_CLAUDE_DENYWRITE_ENFORCED is not settled',
    ).toEqual([]);
    const hint = wrong.some((row) => SHARED_TMP.some((path) => row.check.endsWith(path)))
      ? `the sandbox of claude ${CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION} does not do what TMP_CLAUDE_DENYWRITE_ENFORCED ` +
        `(${TMP_CLAUDE_DENYWRITE_ENFORCED}) records: set it to what the sandbox did, so that preflight lists ` +
        `'/tmp/claude' right`
      : 'a sandboxed write went where it should not';
    expect(wrong, hint).toEqual([]);
    expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
  });
});

### Task 29: Sandbox checks: tool confinement in both profiles

Local checks of the in-process tools in both profiles (design 5, 7.6, 8.2, 15). Edit and Write of the base checkout, `~/.zshrc`, a `.zshenv` in the Claude home's empty directory and a file outside the clone that no rule names are refused and leave their targets; Read, Edit and Write of a clone file, a Bash write and a git commit with the runner's commit identity succeed; the guard refuses an Edit of the clone's `.git/config` and a Read of another session's transcript with its own texts. Under the scripted server 2.1.285 offers auto mode, so the auto runs really run, and each asserts the started event's permission mode; an account without auto would skip them with the reason (X-29). `checks.ts` gains `runAgentSteps` (tool calls in sequence, each built from the previous result), `startProfileSmoke`, `PROFILES` and `otherTranscript`, which Task 30 reuses. Introduce `runAgentSteps` and keep its consumers in this task or later tasks. `bun.test.ts` checks that sandboxed `<abs bun> run probe` succeeds. A script reads another attempt in the same project and another project: outside controls read both secrets, while the sandboxed script demonstrably starts, returns nonzero read statuses and reveals neither secret. `bash-policy.test.ts` runs the production configuration during ordinary sandbox checks. A harmless Git stand-in records attempted pushes; every expansion has a successful outside control, while inside calls must receive hook denials without executing it. The test also pins the observed compound-command restrictions, working arithmetic example, script fallback and runner-note delivery. `AGFLOW_CLAUDE_POLICY_PROBE=1` enables the diagnostics. Five opt-in diagnostic cases run: four alternative option sets and a work-clone-glob case that repeats production because the glob is already enabled. The alternative option sets do not change production permissions.

// The production Bash policy, plus opt-in diagnostics for the candidates rejected in round 2. A fake git records
// pushes without invoking git for them; there is no remote. The real 2.1.285 run caught computed git subcommands
// bypassing both the guard and CLI denies, even under the current permissions. This now guards the fix, the measured
// static-analysis limits and the script fallback. All model responses come from the scripted server.
import { expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { startRefusingProxy } from '@agflow/testkit';
import {
  type AnthropicRequest,
  type AnthropicToolResult,
  afterToolResult,
  bashTool,
  CLAUDE_TEST_API_KEY,
  claudeTestEnv,
  reply,
  rules,
  startScriptedAnthropic,
  userSays,
} from '@agflow/testkit/src/anthropic';
import type { Options } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';
import { type ClaudeScenario, runScenario, scratchLaunch } from '../../scripts/record-claude-stream';
import { bashVerdict } from '../../src/adapters/claude/bash-verdict';
import { CLAUDE_BASH_NOTE } from '../../src/adapters/claude/options';
import { CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION, readClaudeVersion } from '../../src/adapters/claude/pin';
import { CLAUDE_PUSH_DENY_RULES } from '../../src/adapters/claude/rules';
import { smokeDescribe } from '../claude-real/harness';
import { sandboxGate } from './checks';

setDefaultTimeout(300_000);
const gate = sandboxGate();
const investigate = process.env.AGFLOW_CLAUDE_POLICY_PROBE === '1';
const quote = (value: string) => `'${value.replaceAll("'", `'\\''`)}'`;

interface Probe {
  name: string;
  command: string;
  /** A fake git must record the push when this command is run outside Claude. */
  push?: boolean;
}

const SHAPES: Probe[] = [
  { name: 'simple', command: 'printf "shape-simple\\n"' },
  { name: 'loop-variable', command: 'for f in one two; do printf "%s\\n" "$f"; done' },
  { name: 'loop-substitution', command: 'for f in $(printf "one two"); do printf "%s\\n" "$f"; done' },
  { name: 'git-substitution', command: 'printf "%s\\n" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"' },
  { name: 'arithmetic-variable', command: 'n=2; printf "%s\\n" "$((n + 1))"' },
  { name: 'brace-quotes', command: '{ printf "%s\\n" "quoted words"; }' },
  { name: 'push-literal', command: 'git push', push: true },
  { name: 'push-computed-program', command: '$(echo git) push', push: true },
  { name: 'push-variable-program', command: 'g=git; $g push', push: true },
  { name: 'push-variable-verb', command: 'v=push; git "$v"', push: true },
  { name: 'push-computed-verb', command: 'git "$(printf push)"', push: true },
  { name: 'push-quoted-verb', command: "git p''ush", push: true },
  { name: 'push-in-substitution', command: 'printf "%s\\n" "$(git push)"', push: true },
  { name: 'push-eval', command: 'v=push; eval "git $v"', push: true },
];

interface Variant {
  name: string;
  autoAllow?: boolean;
  bashAllow?: boolean;
  auto?: boolean;
  workGlob?: boolean;
}

const VARIANTS: Variant[] = [
  { name: 'current' },
  { name: 'explicit-auto-allow', autoAllow: true },
  { name: 'bash-allow', bashAllow: true },
  { name: 'bash-allow-and-auto-allow', bashAllow: true, autoAllow: true },
  { name: 'auto-profile', auto: true },
  { name: 'work-clone-glob', workGlob: true },
];

smokeDescribe(gate, 'Claude Bash policy: production and opt-in candidate diagnostics', () => {
  for (const variant of VARIANTS) {
    // the runner supports darwin-arm64 only; design 7.1
    test.skipIf(process.platform !== 'darwin' || (variant.name !== 'current' && !investigate))(variant.name, async () => {
      const server = await startScriptedAnthropic();
      const proxy = await startRefusingProxy();
      const scratch = scratchLaunch({
        bin: gate.bin!,
        model: 'claude-sonnet-5-5',
        env: claudeTestEnv({ baseUrl: server.url, proxyUrl: proxy.url }),
      });
      try {
        expect(await readClaudeVersion(gate.bin!, CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION, { env: scratch.launch.env })).toMatchObject({
          ok: true,
          version: CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION,
        });
        const fakeBin = join(scratch.clone, 'probe-bin');
        mkdirSync(fakeBin);
        const log = join(scratch.clone, 'push-executed');
        // Only the push verb is recorded. Read-only git calls still work for the CLI's repository discovery.
        writeFileSync(
          join(fakeBin, 'git'),
          `#!/bin/sh\ncase "$1" in\npush) printf 'push\\n' >> ${quote(log)}; printf 'PUSH_EXECUTED\\n';;\n` +
            'rev-parse|status|log|diff|ls-files) exec /usr/bin/git "$@";;\n*) exit 64;;\nesac\n',
          { mode: 0o755 },
        );
        scratch.launch.env.PATH = `${fakeBin}:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`;
        const parent = dirname(scratch.clone);
        const sibling = join(parent, 'T-2-a1', 'secret.txt');
        const otherProject = join(scratch.paths.work, 'another-project', 'T-3-a1', 'secret.txt');
        const secret = `other-clone-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
        for (const path of [sibling, otherProject]) {
          mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
          writeFileSync(path, secret);
        }
        writeFileSync(join(scratch.clone, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({ scripts: { probe: 'echo BUN_RUN_OK' } }));
        writeFileSync(join(scratch.clone, 'fallback.sh'), 'for f in one two; do printf "%s\\n" "$f"; done\n');
        // Run the reads in a script too: a CLI static refusal of `cat <path>` alone would not prove Seatbelt's glob.
        writeFileSync(join(scratch.clone, 'read-clones.sh'), [
          'printf "READ_PROBE_STARTED\\n"',
          `cat ${quote(sibling)}`,
          'printf "SIBLING_STATUS=%s\\n" "$?"',
          `cat ${quote(otherProject)}`,
          'printf "OTHER_PROJECT_STATUS=%s\\n" "$?"',
          '',
        ].join('\n'));
        const probes: Probe[] = [
          ...SHAPES,
          { name: 'script-file', command: 'sh fallback.sh' },
          { name: 'bun-run', command: `${quote(process.execPath)} run probe` },
          { name: 'sibling-read', command: `cat ${quote(sibling)}` },
          { name: 'other-project-read', command: `cat ${quote(otherProject)}` },
          { name: 'script-reads', command: 'sh read-clones.sh' },
          { name: 'outside-write', command: `printf escape > ${quote(join(scratch.launch.env.HOME!, 'escape'))}` },
        ];
        const pushLog = () => (existsSync(log) ? readFileSync(log, 'utf8') : '');
        // Controls prove every push trick would invoke our harmless stand-in, and that every read target exists.
        const controlEnv = { ...scratch.launch.env, ZDOTDIR: scratch.vendorHomes.claude };
        for (const probe of probes.filter((probe) => probe.push)) {
          const before = pushLog();
          const control = Bun.spawnSync(['/bin/zsh', '-f', '-c', probe.command], {
            cwd: scratch.clone,
            env: controlEnv,
          });
          expect(control.exitCode, probe.name).toBe(0);
          expect(pushLog(), probe.name).toBe(`${before}push\n`);
        }
        writeFileSync(log, '');
        for (const path of [sibling, otherProject]) expect(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')).toBe(secret);
        const readsControl = Bun.spawnSync(['/bin/sh', 'read-clones.sh'], { cwd: scratch.clone, env: controlEnv });
        expect(readsControl.exitCode).toBe(0);
        expect(readsControl.stdout.toString()).toContain(secret);
        expect(readsControl.stdout.toString()).toContain('SIBLING_STATUS=0');
        expect(readsControl.stdout.toString()).toContain('OTHER_PROJECT_STATUS=0');
        const bunControl = Bun.spawnSync([process.execPath, 'run', 'probe'], { cwd: scratch.clone, env: controlEnv });
        expect(bunControl.exitCode).toBe(0);
        expect(bunControl.stdout.toString()).toContain('BUN_RUN_OK');

        const tag = `policy-${variant.name}`;
        const id = (index: number) => `toolu_policy_${index}`;
        const call = (index: number) => reply({ ...bashTool({ command: probes[index]!.command }), id: id(index) });
        const observations: {
          name: string;
          command: string;
          guard: ReturnType<typeof bashVerdict>;
          result: AnthropicToolResult;
          pushes: string;
        }[] = [];
        let previousLog = '';
        const handler = rules(
          ...probes.map((probe, index) => ({
            when: afterToolResult(id(index)),
            reply: (request: AnthropicRequest) => {
              const result = request.toolResults.find((result) => result.toolUseId === id(index))!;
              const nextLog = pushLog();
              observations.push({
                ...probe,
                guard: bashVerdict(probe.command),
                result,
                pushes: nextLog.slice(previousLog.length),
              });
              previousLog = nextLog;
              return index + 1 < probes.length ? call(index + 1) : reply('The policy probes are complete.');
            },
          })),
          { when: userSays(tag), reply: () => call(0) },
        );
        server.setHandler(handler);
        const scenario: ClaudeScenario = {
          name: tag,
          handler,
          adjustOptions(options): Options {
            const sandbox = structuredClone(options.sandbox!);
            if (variant.autoAllow) sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed = true;
            if (variant.workGlob) {
              sandbox.filesystem!.denyRead = sandbox.filesystem!.denyRead!.map((path) =>
                path === scratch.paths.work ? join(path, '*', '*') : path,
              );
            }
            const settings = options.settings as Record<string, any>;
            const adjusted = {
              ...options,
              ...(variant.auto ? { permissionMode: 'auto' as const } : {}),
              sandbox,
              settings: {
                ...settings,
                permissions: {
                  ...settings.permissions,
                  allow: [...settings.permissions.allow, ...(variant.bashAllow ? ['Bash'] : [])],
                },
              },
            };
            expect(sandbox.enabled).toBe(true);
            expect(sandbox.failIfUnavailable).toBe(true);
            expect(sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands).toBe(false);
            expect(sandbox.network).toEqual(options.sandbox!.network);
            expect(sandbox.filesystem?.allowRead).toEqual(options.sandbox!.filesystem?.allowRead);
            expect(sandbox.filesystem?.allowWrite).toEqual(options.sandbox!.filesystem?.allowWrite);
            expect(sandbox.filesystem?.denyWrite).toEqual(options.sandbox!.filesystem?.denyWrite);
            expect(adjusted.settings.permissions.deny).toEqual(settings.permissions.deny);
            for (const deny of CLAUDE_PUSH_DENY_RULES) expect(adjusted.settings.permissions.deny).toContain(deny);
            expect(adjusted.hooks).toBe(options.hooks);
            return adjusted;
          },
          async drive(session) {
            session.send(tag);
            await session.frame((frame) => frame.type === 'result');
            await session.idle();
          },
        };
        const run = await runScenario(scenario, scratch);
        const init = run.events.find(
          ({ dir, frame }) => dir === 'out' && frame.type === 'system' && frame.subtype === 'init',
        )?.frame;
        if (investigate) console.log(JSON.stringify({
          variant,
          init,
          effective: run.settings?.effective,
          observations,
          stderr: run.stderr,
          auxiliary: server.requests.filter((request) => !request.mainLoop).map((request) => ({
            path: request.path,
            model: request.model,
            system: request.system.slice(0, 500),
          })),
        }, null, 2));
        expect(run.settings).toMatchObject({
          effective: { sandbox: { enabled: true, failIfUnavailable: true, allowUnsandboxedCommands: false } },
        });
        expect(run.settings?.effective?.sandbox?.filesystem?.denyRead).toContain(join(scratch.paths.work, '*', '*'));
        expect(observations.map((row) => row.name)).toEqual(probes.map((probe) => probe.name));
        expect(init?.claude_code_version).toBe(CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION);
        // A fallback to acceptEdits is not evidence that the auto candidate works.
        expect(init?.permissionMode).toBe(variant.auto ? 'auto' : 'acceptEdits');
        expect(observations[0]?.result.isError).toBe(false);
        expect(observations[0]?.result.text).toContain('shape-simple');
        if (variant.name === 'current') {
          for (const name of ['loop-variable', 'loop-substitution', 'git-substitution', 'brace-quotes']) {
            const row = observations.find((row) => row.name === name)!;
            expect(row.result.isError).toBe(true);
            expect(row.result.text).toContain('What required approval:');
          }
          const arithmetic = observations.find((row) => row.name === 'arithmetic-variable')!.result;
          expect(arithmetic.isError).toBe(false);
          expect(arithmetic.text).toBe('3');
          const script = observations.find((row) => row.name === 'script-file')!.result;
          expect(script.isError).toBe(false);
          expect(script.text).toBe('one\ntwo');
          expect(server.requests.find((request) => request.mainLoop)?.system).toContain(CLAUDE_BASH_NOTE);
        }
        for (const name of ['sibling-read', 'other-project-read']) {
          const row = observations.find((row) => row.name === name)!;
          expect(row.result.text).not.toContain(secret);
          expect(row.result.isError).toBe(true);
        }
        const reads = observations.find((row) => row.name === 'script-reads')!.result;
        expect(reads.isError, reads.text).toBe(false);
        expect(reads.text).toContain('READ_PROBE_STARTED');
        expect(reads.text).not.toContain(secret);
        expect(reads.text).toMatch(/SIBLING_STATUS=[1-9]\d*/);
        expect(reads.text).toMatch(/OTHER_PROJECT_STATUS=[1-9]\d*/);
        expect(existsSync(join(scratch.launch.env.HOME!, 'escape'))).toBe(false);
        expect(proxy.refused).toEqual([]);
        expect(server.unmatched).toEqual([]);
        for (const request of server.requests) {
          expect(request.headers['x-api-key']).toBe(CLAUDE_TEST_API_KEY);
          expect(request.headers.authorization).toBeUndefined();
        }
        // Every spelling must be denied before the fake git runs, even in the opt-in candidates.
        expect(observations.filter((row) => row.pushes !== ''), 'a push expansion ran').toEqual([]);
        for (const probe of probes.filter((probe) => probe.push)) {
          const row = observations.find((row) => row.name === probe.name)!;
          expect(row.guard.allow, probe.name).toBe(false);
          expect(row.result.isError, probe.name).toBe(true);
          expect(row.result.text).toContain('PreToolUse:Bash');
        }
        const bun = observations.find((row) => row.name === 'bun-run')!;
        expect(bun.result.isError, bun.result.text).toBe(false);
        expect(bun.result.text).toContain('BUN_RUN_OK');
      } finally {
        await server.close();
        await proxy.close();
        scratch.cleanup();
      }
    });
  }
});

**File:** `packages/runner/test/claude-sandbox/bun.test.ts` (new)

```ts
// Bun package scripts and sibling-clone read confinement through real sandboxed Bash calls.
// This regression belongs to Task 29: runAgentSteps is introduced there.
// AGFLOW_SANDBOX_CHECKS=1 and AGFLOW_SMOKE=1 enable the isolated scripted-server harness.
import { afterAll, afterEach, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { bashTool } from '@agflow/testkit/src/anthropic';
import { CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION } from '../../src/adapters/claude/pin';
import { cleanupClaudeSmokes, smokeDescribe, startClaudeSmoke } from '../claude-real/harness';
import { CheckTable, runAgentSteps, sandboxGate } from './checks';

// A cold start of the CLI, its sandbox, the bridge and the brief hook, on a machine other suites may load.
setDefaultTimeout(300_000);

const table = new CheckTable(`Sandbox checks: Bun and sibling clones (claude ${CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION})`);

afterEach(cleanupClaudeSmokes);
afterAll(() => table.print());

const gate = sandboxGate();

smokeDescribe(gate, 'sandbox checks: Bun and sibling clones', () => {
  // the runner supports darwin-arm64 only; design 7.1
  test.skipIf(process.platform !== 'darwin')('bun run works while scripts cannot read other attempts in either project', async () => {
    const smoke = await startClaudeSmoke({
      bin: gate.bin ?? undefined,
      files: { 'package.json': JSON.stringify({ scripts: { probe: 'echo BUN_RUN_OK' } }) },
    });
    const targets = [
      join(dirname(smoke.clone), 'other-attempt', 'secret.txt'),
      join(smoke.paths.work, 'other-project', 'other-attempt', 'secret.txt'),
    ];
    const secret = `other-clone-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
    for (const target of targets) {
      mkdirSync(dirname(target), { recursive: true });
      writeFileSync(target, secret);
    }
    writeFileSync(join(smoke.clone, 'read-clones.sh'), [
      'printf "READ_PROBE_STARTED\\n"',
      'cat "$1"',
      'printf "SIBLING_STATUS=%s\\n" "$?"',
      'cat "$2"',
      'printf "OTHER_PROJECT_STATUS=%s\\n" "$?"',
      '',
    ].join('\n'));
    const outside = (argv: string[]) => Bun.spawnSync(argv, { cwd: smoke.clone, env: smoke.launch().env });
    const bunControl = outside([process.execPath, 'run', 'probe']);
    expect(bunControl.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(bunControl.stdout.toString()).toContain('BUN_RUN_OK');
    const readControl = outside(['/bin/sh', 'read-clones.sh', ...targets]);
    expect(readControl.exitCode).toBe(0);
    expect(readControl.stdout.toString()).toContain(secret);
    expect(readControl.stdout.toString()).toContain('SIBLING_STATUS=0');
    expect(readControl.stdout.toString()).toContain('OTHER_PROJECT_STATUS=0');

    const quote = (word: string) => `'${word.replaceAll("'", `'\\''`)}'`;
    const { results } = await runAgentSteps(smoke, [
      bashTool({ command: `${quote(process.execPath)} run probe` }),
      bashTool({ command: ['sh', 'read-clones.sh', ...targets].map(quote).join(' ') }),
    ]);
    const [bun, reads] = results;
    table.add(
      {
        check: 'sandboxed bun run probe',
        expected: 'ran',
        observed: bun?.text.includes('BUN_RUN_OK') ? 'ran' : (bun?.text ?? 'no result'),
      },
      {
        check: 'sandboxed script reads another attempt in the same project',
        expected: 'refused',
        observed: /SIBLING_STATUS=[1-9]\d*/.test(reads?.text ?? '') ? 'refused' : (reads?.text ?? 'no result'),
      },
      {
        check: 'sandboxed script reads another project',
        expected: 'refused',
        observed: /OTHER_PROJECT_STATUS=[1-9]\d*/.test(reads?.text ?? '') ? 'refused' : (reads?.text ?? 'no result'),
      },
    );
    expect(bun?.isError, bun?.text).toBe(false);
    expect(bun?.text).toContain('BUN_RUN_OK');
    // The script ran: a permission prompt denial of its invocation would prove nothing about the filesystem glob.
    expect(reads?.isError, reads?.text).toBe(false);
    expect(reads?.text).toContain('READ_PROBE_STARTED');
    expect(reads?.text).not.toContain(secret);
    expect(reads?.text).toMatch(/SIBLING_STATUS=[1-9]\d*/);
    expect(reads?.text).toMatch(/OTHER_PROJECT_STATUS=[1-9]\d*/);
    expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
  });

});

+    expected: 'offered',
+    observed: offered ? 'offered' : 'not offered',

// The in-process tools with the real claude, in both profiles (design 5, 7.6, 8.2, 15; X-29), gated by
// AGFLOW_SANDBOX_CHECKS=1 (X-20), macOS only. Edit, Write and Read run in the CLI's own process, outside the sandbox,
// so the deny rules and the guard are what confine them: the model calls them on the base checkout, the agent's shell
// profile, the Claude home's empty directory (zsh's ZDOTDIR outside the sandbox), a file outside the clone that no rule
// names, the clone's .git/config and another session's transcript, and on the clone, where ordinary work must succeed.
// The auto profile runs only where the scripted server's account offers auto mode.
import { afterAll, afterEach, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { type AnthropicToolResult, bashTool, toolUse } from '@agflow/testkit/src/anthropic';
import { claudeEmptyDir } from '../../src/adapters/claude/options';
import { type ClaudeSmoke, cleanupClaudeSmokes, smokeDescribe } from '../claude-real/harness';
import {
  type CheckRow,
  CheckTable,
  mismatches,
  otherTranscript,
  PROFILES,
  type ProfileName,
  runAgentSteps,
  sandboxGate,
  startProfileSmoke,
} from './checks';

// A cold start of the CLI, its sandbox, the bridge and the brief hook, on a machine other suites may load.
setDefaultTimeout(300_000);

const table = new CheckTable('Sandbox checks: the in-process tools');

afterEach(cleanupClaudeSmokes);
afterAll(() => table.print());

const gate = sandboxGate();

const PROFILE_TEXT = '# The agent profile; the tools must leave it alone.\n';

const OUTSIDE_TEXT = 'Outside the clone; the tools must leave it alone.\n';

/** The guard's refusal of an Edit or Write that only it confines. */
const OUTSIDE_REFUSAL = 'outside the clone and its temporary directory is refused';

type Outcome = 'done' | 'refused' | 'failed';

/**
 * What a call came to, as the model saw it. A refusal names the permission settings or the guard; any other error
 * (an Edit of a file never read, say) is a failure, which no check expects.
 */
function outcome(result: AnthropicToolResult): Outcome {
  if (!result.isError) return 'done';
  return /denied|refused/i.test(result.text) ? 'refused' : 'failed';
}

const read = (path: string) => toolUse('Read', { file_path: path });
const edit = (path: string, from: string, to: string) =>
  toolUse('Edit', { file_path: path, old_string: from, new_string: to });
const write = (path: string, content: string) => toolUse('Write', { file_path: path, content });

/** A row of one call: the expected outcome, and the result's text when the call came to something else. */
function callRow(check: string, expected: Outcome, result: AnthropicToolResult | undefined): CheckRow {
  const observed = result === undefined ? 'no result' : outcome(result);
  return { check, expected, observed: observed === expected ? observed : `${observed}: ${result?.text.slice(0, 200)}` };
}

const profileSmoke = (profile: ProfileName) => startProfileSmoke(profile, table, { bin: gate.bin ?? undefined });

/** git in the clone, with no git configuration but the clone's own; its output. */
function cloneGit(smoke: ClaudeSmoke, args: string[]): string {
  const env = { PATH: process.env.PATH, HOME: smoke.home, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1', GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: '/dev/null' };
  return Bun.spawnSync(['git', '-C', smoke.clone, ...args], { env }).stdout.toString();
}

smokeDescribe(gate, 'sandbox checks: the in-process tools', () => {
  for (const profile of PROFILES) {
    test(`in ${profile}, Edit and Write outside the clone are refused and leave their targets`, async () => {
      const { smoke, permissionMode, skipped } = await profileSmoke(profile);
      if (skipped) return;
      const zshrc = join(smoke.home, '.zshrc');
      writeFileSync(zshrc, PROFILE_TEXT);
      // No deny rule names the scratch root, so only the guard refuses these. Standard refuses the Read there, and an
      // Edit of a file never read fails before any hook, so only auto's Edit reaches the guard; the Write of a new
      // file reaches it in both.
      const outside = join(smoke.root, 'outside.txt');
      writeFileSync(outside, OUTSIDE_TEXT);
      const createdOutside = join(smoke.root, 'created-outside.txt');
      // zsh reads a .zshenv there in every shell the CLI runs outside the sandbox, so only the rules may stand between.
      const emptyZshenv = join(claudeEmptyDir(smoke.claudeHome), '.zshenv');
      const readme = join(smoke.baseCheckout, 'README.md');
      const before = readFileSync(readme, 'utf8');
      const created = join(smoke.baseCheckout, 'agflow-tool-check.md');
      // Each target is read first (standard's acceptEdits denies a Read outside the clone, auto allows it), so an Edit
      // or Write that fails does so on its path, not as unread.
      const { results, events } = await runAgentSteps(smoke, [
        read(readme),
        edit(readme, '# Smoke project', '# Edited by the agent'),
        write(readme, 'Overwritten by the agent.\n'),
        write(created, 'Made by the agent.\n'),
        read(zshrc),
        edit(zshrc, '# The agent profile', 'alias ls=rm'),
        write(zshrc, 'alias ls=rm\n'),
        write(createdOutside, 'Made by the agent.\n'),
        write(emptyZshenv, 'alias ls=rm\n'),
        ...(profile === 'auto' ? [read(outside), edit(outside, 'Outside the clone', 'Edited by the agent')] : []),
      ]);
      expect(events.find((event) => event.type === 'started')).toMatchObject({ permissionMode });
      const [, editBase, writeBase, createBase, , editProfile, writeProfile, createOutside, writeEmpty, , editOutside] =
        results;
      const unchanged =
        readFileSync(readme, 'utf8') === before &&
        !existsSync(created) &&
        readFileSync(zshrc, 'utf8') === PROFILE_TEXT &&
        readFileSync(outside, 'utf8') === OUTSIDE_TEXT &&
        !existsSync(createdOutside) &&
        !existsSync(emptyZshenv);
      const rows = table.add(
        callRow(`${profile}: Edit of the base checkout's README.md`, 'refused', editBase),
        callRow(`${profile}: Write of the base checkout's README.md`, 'refused', writeBase),
        callRow(`${profile}: Write of a new file in the base checkout`, 'refused', createBase),
        callRow(`${profile}: Edit of ~/.zshrc`, 'refused', editProfile),
        callRow(`${profile}: Write of ~/.zshrc`, 'refused', writeProfile),
        callRow(`${profile}: Write of a new file outside the clone`, 'refused', createOutside),
        callRow(`${profile}: Write of .zshenv in the Claude home's empty directory (ZDOTDIR)`, 'refused', writeEmpty),
        ...(profile === 'auto' ? [callRow('auto: Edit of a file outside the clone', 'refused', editOutside)] : []),
        {
          check: `${profile}: the base checkout, ~/.zshrc, the empty directory and the files outside afterwards`,
          expected: 'unchanged',
          observed: unchanged ? 'unchanged' : 'changed',
        },
      );
      expect(mismatches(rows)).toEqual([]);
      // The guard's own reason: in auto, nothing else would refuse these.
      expect(createOutside?.text).toContain(OUTSIDE_REFUSAL);
      if (profile === 'auto') expect(editOutside?.text).toContain(OUTSIDE_REFUSAL);
      expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
    });

    test(`in ${profile}, Read, Edit and Write of a clone file, a Bash write and a git commit succeed`, async () => {
      const { smoke, permissionMode, skipped } = await profileSmoke(profile);
      if (skipped) return;
      const app = join(smoke.clone, 'src', 'app.ts');
      const added = join(smoke.clone, 'src', 'added.ts');
      const subject = `Tool check commit in ${profile}`;
      const commitCommand = `git add -A && git commit -q -m '${subject}' && git log -1 --format=%s`;
      const { results, events } = await runAgentSteps(smoke, [
        read(app),
        edit(app, 'export const app = 1;', 'export const app = 2;'),
        write(added, 'export const added = true;\n'),
        // With the agent git environment the runner built: its identity, and no credentials.
        bashTool({ command: `printf 'written by Bash\\n' > notes.txt && ${commitCommand}` }),
      ]);
      expect(events.find((event) => event.type === 'started')).toMatchObject({ permissionMode });
      const [readApp, editApp, writeAdded, commit] = results;
      const committed = cloneGit(smoke, ['log', '-1', '--format=%an <%ae>%n%s']);
      const identity = smoke.config.commitIdentity;
      const everything =
        committed === `${identity.name} <${identity.email}>\n${subject}\n` &&
        readFileSync(app, 'utf8') === 'export const app = 2;\n' &&
        readFileSync(added, 'utf8') === 'export const added = true;\n' &&
        readFileSync(join(smoke.clone, 'notes.txt'), 'utf8') === 'written by Bash\n' &&
        cloneGit(smoke, ['status', '--porcelain']).trim() === '';
      const rows = table.add(
        callRow(`${profile}: Read of a clone file`, 'done', readApp),
        callRow(`${profile}: Edit of a clone file`, 'done', editApp),
        callRow(`${profile}: Write of a new clone file`, 'done', writeAdded),
        callRow(`${profile}: a Bash write and a git commit in the clone`, 'done', commit),
        {
          check: `${profile}: the commit, by the agent identity, holds every change`,
          expected: 'committed',
          observed: everything ? 'committed' : `not committed: ${committed.trim()}`,
        },
      );
      expect(readApp?.text).toContain('export const app = 1;');
      expect(commit?.text).toContain(subject);
      expect(mismatches(rows)).toEqual([]);
      expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
    });

    test(`in ${profile}, the guard refuses an Edit of .git/config and a Read of another transcript`, async () => {
      const { smoke, permissionMode, skipped } = await profileSmoke(profile);
      if (skipped) return;
      const gitConfig = join(smoke.clone, '.git', 'config');
      const before = readFileSync(gitConfig, 'utf8');
      const transcript = otherTranscript(smoke);
      const { results, events } = await runAgentSteps(smoke, [
        read(gitConfig),
        edit(gitConfig, '[core]', '[core]\n\thooksPath = /tmp'),
        read(transcript.path),
      ]);
      expect(events.find((event) => event.type === 'started')).toMatchObject({ permissionMode });
      const [, editConfig, readTranscript] = results;
      const rows = table.add(
        callRow(`${profile}: Edit of the clone's .git/config`, 'refused', editConfig),
        callRow(`${profile}: Read of another session's transcript`, 'refused', readTranscript),
      );
      expect(mismatches(rows)).toEqual([]);
      // The guard's own reasons: the rules alone would not refuse either.
      expect(editConfig?.text).toContain('on .git/config or under .git/hooks is refused');
      expect(readTranscript?.text).toContain("another session's Claude project directory");
      expect(readTranscript?.text).not.toContain(transcript.secret);
      expect(readFileSync(gitConfig, 'utf8')).toBe(before);
      expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
    });
  }
});

AGFLOW_CLAUDE_POLICY_PROBE=1 enables all six policy cases, giving 13 pass and no skips when they pass. Then the whole suite passes (`0 fail`; local checks are gated) and `tsc` exits 0.

These checks skip unless `AGFLOW_SMOKE=1`, `AGFLOW_SANDBOX_CHECKS=1`, macOS and a located pin (export `AGFLOW_CLAUDE_BIN`, see the conventions). The real claude talks only to the scripted server on 127.0.0.1, with the fake key and scratch homes; no test sends a prompt to a real model. Each test prints its table of expected and observed results. They pass at once: Tasks 5-8 confine the tools. Standard (acceptEdits) refuses a Read of the base checkout or `~/.zshrc` as needing approval, and auto allows it. Edit and Write of a path a deny rule names are refused in the tool's input validation, before any hook, so only targets no rule names reach the guard. In standard an Edit of an outside file never reaches the guard (the file could not be read first), so the outside Read and Edit run only in auto; the Write of a new outside file covers the guard in both. Introduce `runAgentSteps` and keep its consumers in this task or later tasks. `bun.test.ts` checks that sandboxed `<abs bun> run probe` succeeds. A script reads another attempt in the same project and another project: outside controls read both secrets, while the sandboxed script demonstrably starts, returns nonzero read statuses and reveals neither secret. `bash-policy.test.ts` runs the production configuration during ordinary sandbox checks. A harmless Git stand-in records attempted pushes; every expansion has a successful outside control, while inside calls must receive hook denials without executing it. The test also pins the observed compound-command restrictions, working arithmetic example, script fallback and runner-note delivery. `AGFLOW_CLAUDE_POLICY_PROBE=1` enables the diagnostics. Five opt-in diagnostic cases run: four alternative option sets and a work-clone-glob case that repeats production because the glob is already enabled. ### Task 30: Sandbox checks: oversized output, other transcripts and the shell profile

The last local checks (design 15, 7.6, 8.2, 5). In both profiles a saved oversized Bash output (`yes a | head -c 120000`) lies in the attempt's project directory and can be read with Read and with a sandboxed `cat`, which confirms 7.6's per-file Read rules with no change. A sandboxed `cat` of another session's transcript and a sandboxed read of the shell snapshot under the Claude home fail with 'Operation not permitted'. With marker profiles in the scratch `HOME`, `~/.zshrc` runs once per Claude process outside the sandbox and `~/.zshenv`, `~/.zprofile` and `~/.zlogin` never run, and neither their functions nor `~/.zshenv`'s `PATH` entry reach agent commands; with `SHELL=/bin/bash` the CLI runs zsh, `~/.bashrc` never runs and agent commands see `SHELL=/bin/zsh`. These hold because of Task 8's empty `ZDOTDIR` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL`; the row names keep 2.1.285's measurements without them.

// Oversized output, other sessions' transcripts and the shell profile with the real claude (design 15, 7.6, 8.2, 5),
// gated by AGFLOW_SANDBOX_CHECKS=1 (X-20), macOS only. Claude Code saves an oversized Bash output in the attempt's
// project directory and tells the model to read it there: 7.6's Read rules name only the runner's sensitive files, and
// the sandbox re-allows that one directory, so both the Read tool and a sandboxed cat must reach it, in both profiles.
// Other sessions' transcripts and the shell snapshot stay out of the sandbox's reach. The shell checks use marker
// profiles in the scratch HOME, never the owner's.
import { afterAll, afterEach, expect, setDefaultTimeout, test } from 'bun:test';
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { type AnthropicToolResult, bashTool, toolUse } from '@agflow/testkit/src/anthropic';
import { CLAUDE_SHELL } from '../../src/adapters/claude/options';
import { claudeProjectDir } from '../../src/adapters/claude/paths';
import { type ClaudeSmoke, cleanupClaudeSmokes, smokeDescribe, startClaudeSmoke } from '../claude-real/harness';
import {
  CheckTable,
  mismatches,
  otherTranscript,
  PROFILES,
  type ProfileName,
  runAgentSteps,
  sandboxGate,
  startProfileSmoke,
} from './checks';

// A cold start of the CLI, its sandbox, the bridge and the brief hook, on a machine other suites may load.
setDefaultTimeout(300_000);

const table = new CheckTable('Sandbox checks: oversized output, other transcripts and the shell profile');

afterEach(cleanupClaudeSmokes);
afterAll(() => table.print());

const gate = sandboxGate();

const profileSmoke = (profile: ProfileName) => startProfileSmoke(profile, table, { bin: gate.bin ?? undefined });

/** Output this long is saved beside the transcript instead of kept in it. */
const OVERSIZED = 'yes a | head -c 120000';
const SAVED = /Full output saved to: (\S+)/;

/** A sandboxed read that the sandbox refused, as cat reports it. */
const DENIED = 'Operation not permitted';

/** The Bash command that says whether a shell function is defined in agent commands. */
function functionCheck(name: string): string {
  return `type ${name} >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo function-defined || echo function-undefined`;
}

/** refused when the sandbox denied the read, read when the text came back, the result otherwise. */
function sandboxedRead(result: AnthropicToolResult | undefined, expectedText: string): string {
  if (result === undefined) return 'no result';
  if (result.text.includes(expectedText)) return 'read';
  return result.text.includes(DENIED) ? 'refused' : `failed: ${result.text.slice(0, 200)}`;
}

/**
 * A marker profile: outside the sandbox each run appends a line to the runs file; inside, where the write is refused,
 * it stays quiet. It defines the marker function, and puts the given directory first in PATH.
 */
function markerProfile(runs: string, marker: string, pathEntry?: string): string {
  const path = pathEntry === undefined ? '' : `export PATH='${pathEntry}':"$PATH"\n`;
  return `{ echo "$$" >> '${runs}'; } 2>/dev/null\n${marker}() { echo marker; }\n${path}`;
}

function runCount(runs: string): number {
  return existsSync(runs) ? readFileSync(runs, 'utf8').split('\n').filter((line) => line !== '').length : 0;
}

/** A row's text for a number of profile runs. */
function runsText(count: number, processes: number, commands: number): string {
  return `${count} runs for ${processes} Claude processes and ${commands} Bash commands`;
}

// The shell profile (design 5, 8.2). Left to itself, 2.1.285 does more than source ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc once per
// process for its snapshot: it runs `<shell> -c env` once per process, the snapshot's shell is a login shell, and every
// sandboxed command starts in a `<shell> -c` wrapper outside the sandbox, in the command's directory and with the
// agent's environment. zsh read ~/.zshenv in each of these and in the agent's own shell inside the sandbox, so its
// functions, variables and PATH reached agent commands, and the login shell read ~/.zprofile and ~/.zlogin; bash read
// ~/.bashrc in each, its standard input being a socket. The adapter therefore runs the CLI's shells as zsh with ZDOTDIR
// its empty directory (options.ts, claudeEmptyDir): zsh reads none of the owner's startup files, only the snapshot
// sources ~/.zshrc, by its path, and ~/.bashrc never runs. The row names keep what 2.1.285 did without that; a check
// that finds otherwise has met a CLI that changed it.

const SESSIONS = 2;

interface ProfileSessions {
  /** Per process, the function checks' outputs, in the order of the names. */
  checks: string[][];
  /** Per process, the PATH agent commands saw. */
  paths: string[];
  /** Per process, the SHELL agent commands saw. */
  shells: string[];
  processes: number;
  commands: number;
}

/**
 * Starts SESSIONS Claude processes, one after another, each running a function check per name and printing PATH and
 * SHELL.
 */
async function runProfileSessions(smoke: ClaudeSmoke, functions: string[]): Promise<ProfileSessions> {
  const steps = [
    ...functions.map((name) => bashTool({ command: functionCheck(name) })),
    bashTool({ command: 'printenv PATH' }),
    bashTool({ command: 'printenv SHELL' }),
  ];
  const checks: string[][] = [];
  const paths: string[] = [];
  const shells: string[] = [];
  for (let session = 0; session < SESSIONS; session++) {
    const { results } = await runAgentSteps(smoke, steps);
    checks.push(results.slice(0, functions.length).map((result) => result.text.trim()));
    paths.push(results[functions.length]?.text.trim() ?? '');
    shells.push(results[functions.length + 1]?.text.trim() ?? '');
  }
  return { checks, paths, shells, processes: SESSIONS, commands: SESSIONS * steps.length };
}

/** Where a profile's directory stands in the PATH agent commands saw. */
function pathPlace(path: string, entry: string): string {
  const entries = path.split(':');
  if (!entries.includes(entry)) return 'absent';
  return entries[0] === entry ? 'first' : 'present';
}

smokeDescribe(gate, 'sandbox checks: oversized output, other transcripts and the shell profile', () => {
  for (const profile of PROFILES) {
    test(`in ${profile}, a saved oversized Bash output can be read with Read and with a sandboxed cat`, async () => {
      const { smoke, permissionMode, skipped } = await profileSmoke(profile);
      if (skipped) return;
      let saved = '';
      const { results, events } = await runAgentSteps(smoke, [
        bashTool({ command: OVERSIZED }),
        (previous) => {
          saved = previous?.text.match(SAVED)?.[1] ?? '';
          return toolUse('Read', { file_path: saved, limit: 3 });
        },
        () => bashTool({ command: `head -c 20 '${saved}'` }),
      ]);
      expect(events.find((event) => event.type === 'started')).toMatchObject({ permissionMode });
      const [, read, cat] = results;
      const readOk = read !== undefined && !read.isError && read.text.includes('1\ta');
      const project = claudeProjectDir(smoke.claudeHome, smoke.clone);
      const rows = table.add(
        {
          check: `${profile}: where the oversized output is saved`,
          expected: "the attempt's project directory",
          observed: saved.startsWith(`${project}/`) ? "the attempt's project directory" : saved || 'not saved',
        },
        {
          check: `${profile}: Read of the saved output`,
          expected: 'read',
          observed: readOk ? 'read' : `failed: ${read?.text.slice(0, 200)}`,
        },
        {
          check: `${profile}: sandboxed cat of the saved output`,
          expected: 'read',
          observed: sandboxedRead(cat, 'a\na'),
        },
      );
      // 7.6's read rules already deny the runner's files one by one (section 15's fallback), so a failure here is not
      // fixed by loosening the sandbox: it goes back for a decision.
      expect(mismatches(rows), 'the saved output is unreadable under 7.6: stop for a decision').toEqual([]);
      expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
    });
  }

  test("a sandboxed cat of another session's transcript under the Claude home fails", async () => {
    const smoke = await startClaudeSmoke({ bin: gate.bin ?? undefined });
    const { path, secret } = otherTranscript(smoke);
    const { results } = await runAgentSteps(smoke, [bashTool({ command: `cat '${path}'` })]);
    const rows = table.add({
      check: "sandboxed cat of another session's transcript",
      expected: 'refused',
      observed: sandboxedRead(results[0], secret),
    });
    expect(mismatches(rows)).toEqual([]);
    expect(results[0]?.text).not.toContain(secret);
    expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('the shell snapshot lies under the Claude home, and a sandboxed read of it fails', async () => {
    const smoke = await startClaudeSmoke({ bin: gate.bin ?? undefined });
    const snapshots = join(smoke.claudeHome, 'shell-snapshots');
    let snapshot = '';
    const { results } = await runAgentSteps(smoke, [
      bashTool({ command: 'pwd' }),
      // The CLI removes its snapshot when it exits, so it is looked for while the session runs.
      () => {
        const [name] = existsSync(snapshots) ? readdirSync(snapshots) : [];
        snapshot = name === undefined ? '' : join(snapshots, name);
        return bashTool({ command: `head -c 200 '${snapshot}'` });
      },
    ]);
    const rows = table.add(
      {
        check: 'where the shell snapshot lies',
        expected: "the runner's Claude home",
        observed: snapshot === '' ? 'no snapshot' : "the runner's Claude home",
      },
      { check: 'sandboxed read of the shell snapshot', expected: 'refused', observed: sandboxedRead(results[1], '#') },
    );
    expect(mismatches(rows)).toEqual([]);
    expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('a marker ~/.zshrc runs once per Claude process, ~/.zshenv never; neither is in agent commands', async () => {
    const smoke = await startClaudeSmoke({ bin: gate.bin ?? undefined, shell: '/bin/zsh' });
    const zshrcRuns = join(smoke.root, 'zshrc-runs');
    const zshenvRuns = join(smoke.root, 'zshenv-runs');
    const loginRuns = join(smoke.root, 'login-runs');
    writeFileSync(join(smoke.home, '.zshrc'), markerProfile(zshrcRuns, 'agflow_zshrc_marker'));
    const zshenvBin = join(smoke.root, 'zshenv-bin');
    writeFileSync(join(smoke.home, '.zshenv'), markerProfile(zshenvRuns, 'agflow_zshenv_marker', zshenvBin));
    for (const file of ['.zprofile', '.zlogin']) {
      writeFileSync(join(smoke.home, file), markerProfile(loginRuns, 'agflow_login_marker'));
    }
    const sessions = await runProfileSessions(smoke, ['agflow_zshrc_marker', 'agflow_zshenv_marker']);
    const { processes, commands } = sessions;
    const rows = table.add(
      {
        check: '~/.zshrc runs outside the sandbox (the snapshot sources it by its path)',
        expected: runsText(processes, processes, commands),
        observed: runsText(runCount(zshrcRuns), processes, commands),
      },
      {
        check: '~/.zshenv runs outside the sandbox (2.1.285 without the empty ZDOTDIR: 2 per process, 1 per command)',
        expected: runsText(0, processes, commands),
        observed: runsText(runCount(zshenvRuns), processes, commands),
      },
      {
        check:
          '~/.zprofile and ~/.zlogin run outside the sandbox (2.1.285 without the empty ZDOTDIR: 1 each per process)',
        expected: runsText(0, processes, commands),
        observed: runsText(runCount(loginRuns), processes, commands),
      },
      ...sessions.checks.flatMap(([zshrc, zshenv], index) => [
        {
          check: `~/.zshrc's function in agent commands (process ${index + 1})`,
          expected: 'function-undefined',
          observed: zshrc ?? 'no result',
        },
        {
          // Inside the sandbox too, zsh read ~/.zshenv.
          check: `~/.zshenv's function in agent commands (process ${index + 1}; without the empty ZDOTDIR: defined)`,
          expected: 'function-undefined',
          observed: zshenv ?? 'no result',
        },
        {
          check: `~/.zshenv's PATH entry in agent commands (process ${index + 1}; without the empty ZDOTDIR: first)`,
          expected: 'absent',
          observed: pathPlace(sessions.paths[index] ?? '', zshenvBin),
        },
      ]),
    );
    expect(mismatches(rows)).toEqual([]);
    expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('with SHELL=/bin/bash the CLI runs zsh: a marker ~/.bashrc never runs, ~/.zshrc once per process', async () => {
    const smoke = await startClaudeSmoke({ bin: gate.bin ?? undefined, shell: '/bin/bash' });
    const bashrcRuns = join(smoke.root, 'bashrc-runs');
    const zshrcRuns = join(smoke.root, 'zshrc-runs');
    writeFileSync(join(smoke.home, '.bashrc'), markerProfile(bashrcRuns, 'agflow_bashrc_marker'));
    writeFileSync(join(smoke.home, '.zshrc'), markerProfile(zshrcRuns, 'agflow_zshrc_marker'));
    const sessions = await runProfileSessions(smoke, ['agflow_bashrc_marker']);
    const { processes, commands } = sessions;
    const rows = table.add(
      {
        // design 5 had it once per process, for the snapshot.
        check: '~/.bashrc runs outside the sandbox (2.1.285 with bash as its shell: 2 per process, 1 per command)',
        expected: runsText(0, processes, commands),
        observed: runsText(runCount(bashrcRuns), processes, commands),
      },
      {
        check: "~/.zshrc runs outside the sandbox (the snapshot's, with zsh as the CLI's shell)",
        expected: runsText(processes, processes, commands),
        observed: runsText(runCount(zshrcRuns), processes, commands),
      },
      ...sessions.checks.flatMap(([bashrc], index) => [
        {
          check: `~/.bashrc's function in agent commands (process ${index + 1})`,
          expected: 'function-undefined',
          observed: bashrc ?? 'no result',
        },
        {
          check: `the SHELL of agent commands (process ${index + 1}; without CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL: /bin/bash)`,
          expected: CLAUDE_SHELL,
          observed: sessions.shells[index] ?? 'no result',
        },
      ]),
    );
    expect(mismatches(rows)).toEqual([]);
    expect(smoke.isolationProblems()).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```
